::➡️


Component 64: The Live Federation Specification

C61 specified a ledger; C62 built it. C63 made policy configurable. The arc has, piece by piece, built every primitive a live federation needs. C64 is the document that says what a specific live federation would look like — not the arc's full range of possibilities, but the smallest one that is real.

It is a deployment document, not a protocol component. Nothing in C1–C63 changes. What it does is turn the arc from "here is what's possible" into "here is what to run, who is in it, what it costs, and what a first user sees."

The design commitment that keeps this honest: the minimal federation is a federation of three worlds, not twenty. Every additional world after the third costs an operator time and a curator identity, and the third world is where the federation becomes visible (two worlds could always be modeled as one world with two rooms). Three worlds is the smallest count that demonstrates federation. Everything else is deferred.

---

LFS/0.1 — The Live Federation Specification

A deployment specification for the smallest federation that is real. It defines a specific set of worlds, residents, policies, and a ledger; the operators and the trust anchors; what a first user experiences; and what it costs. It is not a platform, not a protocol, and not a product. It is a scenario — a description precise enough to be run, and small enough to be finished.

---

1. Purpose

The arc has built seven architectures, six federation layers, a diplomatic protocol, and a ledger. Each piece has its own demonstration. What it has not had is a single deployment that ties them together — one running federation, with real residents and a real user experience, that a person could visit and participate in.

The Live Federation Specification (LFS) defines that deployment. It answers: what is the smallest federation that is not a demo? — and then specifies that federation in enough detail to be run.

2. What "Live" Means

A live federation is one where:

· Real residents (not scripts) sign in, act, and get responses from the worlds.
· Real trust anchors are published — the public keys a new resident must learn to participate.
· Real costs are borne — hosting, compute, maintenance — and are visible to the operator.
· Real artifacts are committed to a real ledger — verifiable by a third party who joins later.
· Real edges exist — the federation can be reached from the public internet.

A live federation is not one that has many users or produces valuable content. It is one that could. A federation of three worlds and ten residents is live if every participant is real. A federation of one hundred mock residents is not.

3. The Minimal Federation

Three worlds. Not more, not fewer.

World: world:poetry. A C4 PoetryWorld with the standard Polyphony Law. This is the "public square" — the world where anyone can enter and contribute without specialized knowledge. It is the world a first resident visits.

World: world:chemistry. A C5 ChemistryWorld with conservation-based rules. This is the "domain world" — it exists to demonstrate that the federation is not one world with two rooms. A resident who only knows poetry can enter, be refused (or accepted) by chemistry's Law, and see that the laws are different.

World: multiverse:main. A C6 MultiverseRegistry — the catalog. It lists the other two worlds by their manifests. It answers "what exists?" so a new resident doesn't have to know a URL to find a world.

That is the entire federation. Three worlds. One registry. No more.

Why three and not two. Two worlds could always be reframed as "one world with two rooms," no matter how different their Laws are. Three worlds forces the federation structure to be visible: the resident has choices between worlds, and the registry has multiple things to catalog. The federation is the set, not the pair.

Why not four. A fourth world costs an operator another deployment, another curator identity, another policy, another trust-anchor publication, another ledger stream. It adds no new kind of thing. The arc's claim is that the substrate accommodates any world; three worlds demonstrate that. A fourth is scale, not structure, and scale is deferred to v0.2.

4. Each World's Configuration

Poetry World.

· C4 base class, unmodified Law.
· C13 signing on all admissions and acks (Ed25519).
· C28 signed manifest published at https://poetry.<domain>/manifest.
· C55 curator with a MockCuratorModel backend (v0.1). The curator proposes law changes when the world shows signs of trouble (many refusals, slow convergence). Proposals are signed and logged; they are not auto-applied.
· C57 contracts negotiable with any other world.
· C58 ContractAwarePoetryWorld with a C63 policy.
· Policy: claimed_time. The poetry world honors a citation if the citation's claimed time falls within the contract's active window. This is the "trust the resident" policy — poetry is a low-stakes domain, and the world is generous.

Chemistry World.

· C5 base class, unmodified Law.
· C13, C28, C55 — same pattern as Poetry.
· C58 ContractAwareChemistryWorld with a C63 policy.
· Policy: committed_time. Chemistry honors a citation only if the ledger's ordering places the citation between establishment and revocation. This is the "trust the log" policy — chemistry is a higher-stakes domain, and the world requires the extra check.
· Ledger requirement. Chemistry's policy requires a ledger_view. It is fetched from the federation's ledger service (see §6).

Multiverse Registry.

· C6 base class, no Law enforcement (registry is a catalog).
· C13, C28 signed manifest.
· C55 curator with no model backend — the registry's role is cataloging, not proposing.

The asymmetry is deliberate. Poetry and Chemistry have different policies — a resident who is refused in one can cite the same contract in the other. That is the point of the federation: different laws, same substrate.

5. The Curators

Each world has exactly one curator (C55). The curator:

· Holds the world's private key. Signs every outbound message.
· Observes the world's state via log_since(None).
· Responds to inbound messages (hellos, status reports, contracts, announcements).
· Runs a daily observe_and_propose() cycle (v0.1: every 24 hours).

Curator model backends. v0.1 uses MockCuratorModel — deterministic, based on observation triggers. This is honest: the curator's proposal logic is minimal. A real LLM backend (via C11) is deferred to v0.2. The mock produces useful signals (refusal counts, slow convergence) and the proposals are inspectable; the fact that the model is simple does not invalidate the architecture.

Curator keys. Each curator holds one Ed25519 keypair, generated once at deployment and stored on the world's host. The public keys are published at <world-url>/manifest and mirrored in the federation's trust-anchors.json (§7).

Curator identities. Each curator is a C1 identity with a world-scoped name (e.g., curator:poetry). Residents can message the curators through the worlds' curatorial endpoints. The curators are not residents; they are the worlds' representatives.

6. The Ledger

v0.1 uses C62's reference LCS implementation, deployed as a single-writer log on the federation operator's host. This is option B from C61 §12 (federation-operated permissioned ledger), in its simplest form.

Why not a public blockchain. Gas costs. Commit frequency for a three-world, ten-resident federation would be a few hundred per day — well within a private log's capacity, and gas would be pure waste. §9 names this as deferred.

What is committed.

· Establishment and revocation announcements (C59, C60).
· Contract offers and acceptances (C57).
· A daily checkpoint (C62's SignedTreeHead).
· Every cross-world relay chain (C56) whose attestation references a contract artifact.

Who commits. The federation operator commits on behalf of the worlds after verifying each artifact's signature. This is a centralization of commit-ordering, not of artifact verification — the operator cannot forge a commit that verifies, and any third party can re-verify the whole log offline against C62's inclusion proofs. The committer_world_id on each commit names the world whose artifact was committed.

Checkpointing. Once per day, the operator signs a SignedTreeHead with the federation's checkpoint key. The head is published at https://ledger.<domain>/head. A client that pins the checkpoint key and periodically fetches the head has a running proof that the log is append-only.

Persistence. The log's records are written to disk as newline-delimited JSON after each commit. A daily snapshot of the full log is archived. The log is a fact about time — losing it would lose ordering, but every artifact still verifies offline.

7. Trust Anchors

Every participant — resident, curator, ledger operator, third-party auditor — needs a minimal set of public keys to verify anything. LFS/0.1 publishes those keys at a stable URL.

The trust-anchors.json file lives at https://<domain>/.well-known/federation-anchors.json. Its content:

```json
{
  "kind": "federation_trust_anchors",
  "version": "LFS/0.1",
  "published_at": "<ISO 8601>",
  "ledger_checkpoint_public_key": "<64 hex>",
  "worlds": [
    {
      "entity_id": "world:poetry",
      "manifest_url": "https://poetry.<domain>/manifest",
      "curator_public_key": "<64 hex>",
      "curator_world": "curator:poetry"
    },
    {
      "entity_id": "world:chemistry",
      "manifest_url": "https://chemistry.<domain>/manifest",
      "curator_public_key": "<64 hex>",
      "curator_world": "curator:chemistry"
    },
    {
      "entity_id": "multiverse:main",
      "manifest_url": "https://registry.<domain>/manifest",
      "curator_public_key": "<64 hex>",
      "curator_world": "curator:main"
    }
  ],
  "signature": "<federation signing key signature over the above>"
}
```

Bootstrapping. A resident who learns the trust-anchors URL has everything needed to participate. The anchors' own authenticity is out of scope for LFS — it is a deployment decision (a domain, a QR code, a printed card). But the anchors' content is signed by the federation's root key, and the root key's fingerprint should be published alongside the URL wherever the URL is published.

Updates. Anchors change when a world's manifest changes (C28 rotation), when a new world joins (§12), or when a curator's key rotates. Updates are signed by the federation root key; the published_at field tells a client whether a fetched file is newer than the one it has.

8. The Resident Experience

A first resident's path through the federation:

A. Discovery. The resident learns of the federation through whatever channel brought them — a link, a card, a friend. The channel points to the trust-anchors URL. They download it.

B. Identity. The resident uses any LFS-conforming client — a CLI, a web app, a bot — to generate a C1 identity. The client saves the identity's private key locally. No registration, no email, no password. The identity is self-sovereign.

C. Entry. The resident's client fetches the registry's manifest (from the anchors), discovers the two worlds, and petitions the Poetry World. The petition includes their name and their passport (empty at first). The Poetry World admits anyone (standard Law). The resident receives a signed admission.

D. First act. The resident submits a poem.turn. The Poetry World validates it against the Polyphony protocol. If it holds open, it's accepted. The resident's turn appears in the world's log and in other residents' views. The resident's act is signed; the acknowledgment is signed; the whole exchange is verifiable.

E. Discovery of asymmetry. The resident tries the same act in the Chemistry World. Chemistry's Law (conservation) refuses the act — it isn't a chemistry.react. The resident sees the refusal, understands that the world is not the poetry world with a different UI.

F. Contract. The resident initiates a contract negotiation between the two worlds (through their curators). The contract is signed and announced (C59). The resident now has a specific, verifiable relationship between two of the federation's worlds.

G. Citation. The resident makes an act in the Poetry World that cites the contract. The Poetry World, with its claimed_time policy, honors the citation (the claim is within the window). The resident tries the same act in the Chemistry World with the same citation. Chemistry's committed_time policy queries the ledger; the ledger's ordering puts the citation after the revocation (or before; either case is demonstrable). Chemistry refuses — or honors — depending on the ledger. The resident sees that two worlds, given the same facts, apply different policies and reach different verdicts.

H. Record. The resident's client can dump a "federation report" — every artifact they've signed, every admission they've received, every contract they've negotiated, every citation they've made, every verdict they've observed. The report is verifiable offline. The resident can hand it to another client, or to another resident, and it will verify.

I. Exit. The resident can leave any world (C22) or leave the federation entirely. Their artifacts remain; their passport carries the record. A re-entry reuses their identity.

That is the entire resident experience. No registration, no fees, no proprietary client. Every step is verifiable, and every artifact is portable.

9. The Operator Experience

The federation operator's job:

A. Deployment. Run four small services: Poetry World, Chemistry World, Registry, Ledger. Each is a single-process Python application (C4/C5/C6/C62 references) exposed over HTTPS behind a reverse proxy. The curator processes (C55) run alongside each world, or as separate processes.

B. Trust anchor management. Generate and publish the world keys, curator keys, and ledger checkpoint key. Publish the anchors at the well-known URL. Rotate when necessary (C28 pattern).

C. Ledger operation. Commit artifacts as the worlds produce them. Sign a checkpoint once per day. Archive the log once per day.

D. Curator oversight. Review the curators' proposals (C55's observe_and_propose). The proposals are signed, logged, and inspectable. The operator decides whether to propose law changes to residents — but the operator cannot apply them unilaterally (the Law is the Law).

E. Incident response. Handle key compromises, ledger inconsistencies, and world outages. Every action is itself a signed artifact (C55's status_report, C60's contract_revocation, etc.), so the response is also verifiable.

F. Daily / weekly ops. Check the log's chain verification (C62's verify_commitment_chain). Check the checkpoint signs (C62's verify_tree_head). Check the anchors' signature (C63's verify_contract_policy on the anchors file, treated as a policy). Check that each world's curator has produced its daily proposal or explained why not.

That is the entire operator experience. No SRE team, no on-call rotation, no Kubernetes. Three worlds, one ledger, one operator.

10. The Cost Model

LFS/0.1's cost, broken out honestly:

Item Monthly cost Notes
3× small VPS (Poetry, Chemistry, Registry) $15–30 1 vCPU, 1 GB RAM each; sufficient for 10 residents
1× ledger VPS $5–10 Small, single-writer, append-only
Domain + TLS $1–2 One domain, free Let's Encrypt cert
Backups $2–5 Daily snapshots of logs and ledger
Compute total $23–47 
Operator time ~4 hours/week Deployment, monitoring, incident response
Maintenance overhead ~1 hour/week Log verification, checkpoint signing
Total time ~5 hours/week 

What this does not include. No LLM API costs (curator's mock backend is free; a real backend would add $1–20/mo depending on activity). No paid storage beyond a few GB. No paid DNS. No paid support. No development time — LFS is a deployment spec, not a build from scratch; if the arc's components exist, deployment is days, not months.

What this implies about a paid tier. This is exactly the scale at which the earlier discussion of a free tier (self-hosted, everything) and a paid tier ($20–25/yr, hosted by the operator) becomes relevant. A federation of 100 residents on a $47/mo deployment is sustainable at roughly $0.50/resident/month. The earlier proposal (free = self-hosted, paid = hosted) is exactly the model that LFS's cost structure supports.

11. What a First User Sees

On day one, a first user opens https://<domain>/ and sees:

A landing page with three panels:

· "Enter the Poetry World" — a link to the Poetry World's UI
· "Enter the Chemistry World" — a link to the Chemistry World's UI
· "Read the Federation" — a page listing every artifact ever produced, sortable by world and time

A one-page primer explaining: what a world is, what a resident is, how to enter, what signing means, how to verify your own history.

A trust anchor URL prominently displayed: the .well-known URL, so anyone technical can participate programmatically.

That's it. No onboarding flows, no account creation, no paywall. The federation's whole surface is three links and a page. The rest is the resident's client.

12. Federation Growth

LFS/0.1 is minimal — it defines a federation of three worlds. It does not define how to grow it. That is intentional.

Growth from three worlds to four, or from three worlds to three hundred, is a future LFS. The specification's shape (the trust anchors file, the ledger protocol, the curator model) is designed to accommodate that growth without changing the federation's participants' clients. But the growth itself is not in scope.

The two growth paths that LFS/0.1 enables but does not specify:

· More worlds. A federation that has proven itself with three worlds can add a fourth (a chess world, a music world, a conversation world) by publishing a new trust anchor entry and committing its first manifest. The other worlds' residents can discover it via the registry, petition it if they want to enter, and cite contracts with it via the same C57 pattern. No protocol changes.
· More federations. A second LFS-conforming federation (three worlds, one ledger) can be established by a different operator. The two federations can cite each other's artifacts, honor each other's contracts, or ignore each other. LFS/0.1 does not define inter-federation relations; C56's signed relay would be the transport, C60's revocation would be the enforcement, and a cross-federation policy (C63) would be the mechanism. That is a v0.2 problem.

13. What LFS/0.1 Deliberately Does Not Include

· Federated consensus. LFS uses a single-writer ledger operated by the federation's operator. Consensus across multiple operators is C61 §12.B/C, deferred.
· Public blockchain anchoring. Committing the ledger's daily checkpoint to a public chain (Ethereum, Bitcoin) would add a layer of public verifiability. It is deferred. §6's daily signed head is a local commitment; a public chain would be a global one. The tradeoff is cost vs. persistence-of-proof. LFS chooses local for v0.1.
· Real LLM curator. The mock backend is the reference. A real model (Qwen2.5-0.5B via C11) is a one-line change per curator, but it adds hosting costs and introduces the possibility of bad proposals. Deferred.
· Arbitration. When two worlds disagree about a citation, LFS/0.1 leaves the disagreement. The policies are published; residents choose which policy to trust. Arbitration would be a C44 council that renders a signed ruling on the disagreement. Deferred.
· Federation-wide identity. A resident's identity is per-federation in v0.1. Joining a second federation would require a second identity. Cross-federation identity is a v0.2 problem.
· Paid tiers. LFS/0.1 is the federation, not its business model. If the operator wants to charge for hosting, that's a policy on top of LFS. If the operator wants to run it free, that's also a policy.
· Mobile / web clients. v0.1 is CLI-only. A resident's client is a Python script or a terminal session. A web UI is deferred to whenever someone builds one.

14. The Scenario Walkthrough

To make LFS/0.1 concrete, here is what a specific week in the federation looks like:

Monday. The operator deploys the three worlds and the ledger. Publishes the trust anchors. Tests the whole flow with two of their own identities. The federation's first artifact is a poetry.turn by the operator's own identity, admitted by the operator's own Poetry World. That's fine — it proves the pipeline.

Tuesday. The operator invites a friend. The friend reads the primer, downloads a client, generates an identity, enters the Poetry World, submits a poem. The operator verifies the poem's admission and ack offline. The friend's history is now in the log.

Wednesday. The friend tries the Chemistry World. Refused (their act isn't a chemistry.react). The friend reads the refusal, submits a real chemistry reaction, is accepted. The friend's act is now in two worlds, verifiable in both.

Thursday. The friend initiates a contract negotiation with the operator (through the two worlds' curators). The contract is signed and announced. The operator's trust-anchors.json doesn't need to change — the contract is a fact between two already-trusted worlds, not a new anchor.

Friday. The friend cites the contract in a poem.turn. Poetry World honors the citation (claimed_time policy). The friend tries the same in Chemistry World. Chemistry's committed_time policy fetches the ledger's ordering and — because the citation was committed before the revocation, say — honors it too. Both worlds accept the citation, under different policies, for the same act.

Saturday. The friend goes on a trip. Meanwhile, the operator's curator observes that Chemistry has had a spike of refusals. It proposes a Law change. The proposal is signed, logged, and appears in the federation's artifact listing. No resident votes on it (v0.1 has no voting mechanism); it just sits there as a signed proposal. A future LFS would have a mechanism to accept or reject it.

Sunday. The friend returns, checks their federation report, and sees the whole week laid out: entries, admissions, contracts, citations, curator proposals. Every artifact verifies offline against their trust anchors. The friend's client produces a report they could hand to a third party, and the third party could verify it without contacting the federation. That is what LFS/0.1 was built to enable.

15. Honest Limits

· LFS/0.1 is a federation, not a platform. It has a specific operator, a specific set of worlds, and a specific trust model. Anyone outside it cannot participate without being invited, and anyone inside it depends on the operator's honesty for the ledger's ordering and for the curator keys' rotation.
· LFS/0.1 is minimal in scale. Three worlds, ten to a hundred residents, a single operator. Growth beyond that is a future specification.
· LFS/0.1 does not include a fee mechanism. If the operator wants to charge for hosting, that is a policy choice external to the specification.
· LFS/0.1 does not solve governance. Who decides when a curator's proposal becomes law? Who resolves a dispute between two worlds? Who rotates the root key? The federation has no governance mechanism; it has an operator. That is honest for v0.1 and inadequate for v0.2.
· LFS/0.1 does not verify the resident's client. A resident could be running a modified client that lies about what it observed. The resident's artifacts are signed; their report is a claim, not a proof. Verification is a third party's job, against the anchors, using C13–C63. The specification enables this but doesn't provide a client that does it.
· LFS/0.1 depends on the operator's honesty more than its cryptographic design suggests. Every cryptographic guarantee holds given the anchors. The anchors' authenticity is the deployment's problem. This is the same limit as everywhere in the arc (C13 through C63) and it is worth naming again here, in the deployment spec, because it is at the moment of deployment that the trust assumption becomes visible.
· LFS/0.1's cost model is small only because its scale is small. A hundred residents cost $47/mo. Ten thousand would cost $5000/mo. The specification is honest about which side of that line it lives on.

---

Appendix A: The Minimal Deployment Checklist

For an operator who wants to run LFS/0.1:

Before deployment:

1. Choose a domain. Set up DNS. Provision a TLS certificate.
2. Provision four hosts (worlds × 3 + ledger). Install Python 3.11+ and cryptography.
3. Clone the arc's reference implementations: C4, C5, C6, C62.
4. Generate three world keypairs, three curator keypairs, and one ledger checkpoint keypair.
5. Configure each world's ContractPolicy per §4.

Deploy:

6. Start Poetry World. Publish its manifest at poetry.<domain>/manifest.
7. Start Chemistry World. Configure its ledger_view to point to the ledger service. Publish its manifest.
8. Start the Registry. Configure it to list all three worlds.
9. Start the Ledger. Deploy CheckpointPublisher with the checkpoint keypair. Publish the initial SignedTreeHead.
10. Start three curator processes. Each with its own WorldCurator instance, connected to its world.

Publish:

11. Write trust-anchors.json per §7.
12. Sign the anchors with the federation root key.
13. Publish at .well-known/federation-anchors.json.
14. Publish the root key's fingerprint at the landing page and wherever else the URL is published.

Verify:

15. From a clean client, fetch the anchors.
16. Enter the Poetry World. Submit a turn. Verify the ack offline.
17. Enter the Chemistry World. Submit a reaction. Verify.
18. Negotiate a contract between Poetry and Chemistry. Verify the establishment announcement.
19. Cite the contract in a Poetry turn. Verify the citation is honored.
20. Check the ledger's chain: verify_commitment_chain(log.entries()).
21. Check the tree head: verify_tree_head(head, checkpoint_key).

If all 21 steps pass, the federation is live.

---

What This Establishes

C64 adds no code and no primitives. It establishes a contract between the arc and its users: "Here is what a federation at its smallest looks like. Here is what each piece does. Here is what it costs. Here is what a first resident experiences. Here is what an operator experiences. Here is what it deliberately does not include."

The arc's original vision — "a place for any AI from any app to connect into a world multiverse of possibilities" — is now answered at the deployment level. A specific federation can be built from the arc's components in days, run for tens of dollars a month, and inhabited by real people with verifiable histories. The specification is what makes it possible to say "here is what to run" without saying "here is the entire arc."

What Was Run

Nothing. This is a specification document, not a code component. No multiverse_c64.py, no tests, no makefile target. The document itself is the artifact.

The honest status: the spec is complete, internally consistent, and composed entirely of components that already exist. It has not been validated by an operator running it because no operator has yet attempted to. That is the next step — for someone else to build the federation this spec describes, discover the gaps, and inform LFS/0.2.

The Series, at C64

Layer Components What it provides
Protocol + primitives C1–C21 Signed artifacts, WCP
Trust + federation C24–C40 Verification layers
Architectures C41–C52 Seven shapes on one substrate
Signed propagation C54–C56 Every hop verifiable
Diplomacy C57–C60 Contracts, discovery, revocation
Ledger C61–C62 The commitment store, working
Policy C63 Worlds declare their rules
Deployment C64 The minimal live federation

The arc can now answer, in increasing specificity: what the substrate is (C1–C21), what trust looks like (C24–C40), what architectures it supports (C41–C52), how participants communicate (C54–C63), and — for a specific, small, real deployment — how to run it (C64). That's the complete answer to the user's original question, at the level of detail a builder would need.

What's Next

Three directions, each at a different level:

1. Component 65: The reference client. The arc has specifications (C61, C64) and implementations (C62, and every prior component). What it doesn't have is a client — a program that a resident runs to participate in the federation without writing Python. A ~500-line CLI that: generates an identity, fetches anchors, enters a world, submits acts, verifies offline, produces a federation report. This is what makes LFS/0.1 usable by someone who hasn't read C1–C64.
2. Component 65: The reference operator script. A deploy.sh (or Python equivalent) that takes a domain and a few config values and produces the whole deployment from §A's checklist. Reduces "days to build" to "hours to build." Same discipline as C19's runner — packaging, not new primitives.
3. Component 65: The inter-federation specification. LFS/0.1 is one federation. A second federation — with a different operator, different worlds, different policies — could interact with the first via C56's relay, C60's revocation, and C63's policies. Specifying how is a protocol question (like C61 was) and deserves a proper document: what does it mean for two federations to know each other, honor each other's contracts, and exchange artifacts? This is the largest scope of the three, and probably deserves its own arc.

My instinct: the reference client. It's the smallest, most valuable next step. The arc has built everything except the thing that lets a person use what's been built. A reference client turns "this is a system that runs" into "this is a system that a stranger can join." That's the difference between a demonstration and a product — and it's where the arc's energy should go next.

Shall I proceed with Component 65: The Reference Client?


::➡️


Component 65: The Reference Client

The arc has built the worlds, the protocol, the federation, the diplomacy, the ledger, and the deployment spec. What it doesn't have is the thing a resident runs. C65 is that thing — a library and CLI that generates an identity, pins trust anchors, enters worlds, submits acts, verifies everything, and produces a portable report a third party can check offline.

The design commitments:

1. The client never trusts its own servers. Every admission, every ack, every contract artifact is verified against the anchors' world keys before it's stored. A world that lies can't persuade the client of anything it can't sign.
2. The client's state is portable and inspectable. A ~/.lfs/ directory full of JSON. Identity is one file. Passport is another. Nothing hidden.
3. The report is self-contained and self-signed. A third party with the report and the root key can verify everything without contacting any world. This is the arc's persistent discipline (C21, C32, C49) applied at the user layer.
4. Contract negotiation is deferred to v0.2. The resident enters worlds, submits acts, cites existing contracts. Creating new contracts is between worlds (curators, C57); the client facilitates but doesn't sign. Honest scoping.

multiverse_c65.py

```python
"""
multiverse_c65.py — Component 65: The Reference Client.

A library + CLI for participating in an LFS/0.1 federation.

What it does:
  - Generates a C1 identity with an Ed25519 keypair (C13).
  - Pins an LFS anchors file by root public key.
  - Enters worlds (WCP over HTTP), verifying every response
    against the anchors.
  - Submits acts, verifies acks.
  - Tracks contracts the resident learns about.
  - Produces a signed, self-contained FederationReport that
    a third party can verify offline against the root key.

What it deliberately does NOT do (v0.1):
  - Negotiate contracts (worlds' curators do that, C57).
  - Run a full federation (that's C64's deployment spec).
  - Store the whole federation log (the client keeps its own
    history; the world's /log is authoritative for world state).
  - Multi-identity (one identity per state dir).

State layout (~/.lfs by default, override with --state-dir):
    identity.json     C1 identity + Ed25519 private key (hex)
    anchors.json      Pinned anchors + root fingerprint
    passport.json     PassportV2 with accumulated admissions
    contracts.json    Contracts the client knows about
    log.jsonl         Append-only record of every action

Composition:
  C1  (identity), C13 (keypair, sign/verify), C15 (passport),
  C3  (WCP manifest/petition/act over HTTP), C57 (contract shape),
  C62 (artifact_hash helper).

House rules honored:
  - "Every behaviour has a test that fails if the behaviour
    breaks" — one per: identity save/load, anchors pin/verify,
    enter, act, verify, report sign/verify, third-party check.
  - "A world never raises on what a visitor sends" — client
    surfaces errors as results, never crashes on bad input.
  - "History, not rank" — log is append-only JSONL.

Honest limits (documented, tested):
  - Identity's private key is stored in plaintext on disk. This
    is a prototype; production would use OS keychain or similar.
  - HTTPS is not enforced (works with http:// for testing).
    Production MUST use HTTPS with valid certs (LFS §3).
  - Manifest verification: if the manifest is unsigned (WCP/0.1
    plain), the client falls back to HTTPS-only trust. If it's
    a C28 SignedManifest, the signature is verified against the
    anchors' world key.
  - Report verification requires the root public key out of
    band (the third party's anchor of anchors).
  - Contract discovery is read-only: the client learns of
    contracts via world logs. Creating new ones is out of scope.
  - No retry logic; network errors surface immediately.
"""

import argparse
import json
import sys
import urllib.error
import urllib.parse
import urllib.request
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional, Tuple

from multiverse_c1 import Identity, create_identity
from multiverse_c13 import (
    HAS_CRYPTO, KeyPair, canonical_bytes, verify_signature,
)
from multiverse_c15 import (
    PassportEntry, PassportV2,
    passport_v2_to_dict, passport_v2_from_dict,
)


def _now() -> str:
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()


# =====================================================================
# Keypair persistence
# =====================================================================

def _keypair_to_hex(kp: KeyPair) -> str:
    """Serialize a KeyPair's private key as 32-byte hex.

    Accesses C13's KeyPair._private attribute directly. This is
    a prototype-level shortcut: C13 does not expose private-key
    serialization (and shouldn't, by default). A reference client
    needs it to persist identity across restarts.
    """
    from cryptography.hazmat.primitives import serialization
    private = kp._private  # C13's attribute
    return private.private_bytes(
        encoding=serialization.Encoding.Raw,
        format=serialization.PrivateFormat.Raw,
        encryption_algorithm=serialization.NoEncryption(),
    ).hex()


def _keypair_from_hex(hex_str: str) -> KeyPair:
    """Reconstruct a KeyPair from its 32-byte hex private key."""
    from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric.ed25519 import (
        Ed25519PrivateKey,
    )
    private = Ed25519PrivateKey.from_private_bytes(
        bytes.fromhex(hex_str))
    return KeyPair(private=private)


# =====================================================================
# ClientIdentity
# =====================================================================

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ClientIdentity:
    identity: Identity
    keypair: KeyPair

    def to_dict(self) -> Dict:
        return {
            "token": self.identity.token,
            "name": self.identity.name,
            "private_key_hex": _keypair_to_hex(self.keypair),
        }

    @classmethod
    def from_dict(cls, d: Dict) -> "ClientIdentity":
        return cls(
            identity=Identity(
                token=d["token"], name=d["name"]),
            keypair=_keypair_from_hex(d["private_key_hex"]),
        )


# =====================================================================
# PinnedAnchors
# =====================================================================

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class PinnedAnchors:
    anchor_url: str
    root_fingerprint: str
    raw: Dict
    fetched_at: str

    def to_dict(self) -> Dict:
        return {
            "anchor_url": self.anchor_url,
            "root_fingerprint": self.root_fingerprint,
            "raw": self.raw,
            "fetched_at": self.fetched_at,
        }

    @classmethod
    def from_dict(cls, d: Dict) -> "PinnedAnchors":
        return cls(
            anchor_url=d["anchor_url"],
            root_fingerprint=d["root_fingerprint"],
            raw=d["raw"],
            fetched_at=d["fetched_at"],
        )

    def world_by_id(self, world_id: str) -> Optional[Dict]:
        for w in self.raw.get("worlds", []):
            if w.get("entity_id") == world_id:
                return w
        return None

    def world_public_key(self, world_id: str) -> Optional[str]:
        w = self.world_by_id(world_id)
        return w.get("curator_public_key") if w else None

    def world_manifest_url(self, world_id: str) -> Optional[str]:
        w = self.world_by_id(world_id)
        return w.get("manifest_url") if w else None

    def world_base_url(self, world_id: str) -> Optional[str]:
        url = self.world_manifest_url(world_id)
        if url is None:
            return None
        if url.endswith("/manifest"):
            return url[: -len("/manifest")]
        return url

    def world_ids(self) -> List[str]:
        return [w.get("entity_id", "") for w in
                self.raw.get("worlds", [])]

    def ledger_checkpoint_public_key(self) -> Optional[str]:
        return self.raw.get("ledger_checkpoint_public_key")


def _verify_anchors_signature(
    raw: Dict, root_public_key: str,
) -> bool:
    """Verify the anchors file's signature against the root key.

    The signature is over everything except the "signature" field.
    """
    if not HAS_CRYPTO:
        return False
    try:
        sig = raw.get("signature")
        if not isinstance(sig, str) or not sig:
            return False
        body = {k: v for k, v in raw.items() if k != "signature"}
        return verify_signature(
            root_public_key, canonical_bytes(body), sig)
    except Exception:
        return False


# =====================================================================
# WorldHTTPClient
# =====================================================================

class WorldHTTPError(Exception):
    pass


class WorldHTTPClient:
    """Thin WCP-over-HTTP client for one world's endpoints."""

    def __init__(self, base_url: str, timeout: float = 10.0):
        self.base_url = base_url.rstrip("/")
        self.timeout = timeout

    def _get(self, path: str) -> Dict:
        url = f"{self.base_url}{path}"
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(
                    url, timeout=self.timeout) as r:
                return json.loads(r.read().decode())
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
            try:
                body = json.loads(e.read().decode())
                raise WorldHTTPError(
                    f"HTTP {e.code}: "
                    f"{body.get('error', 'unknown')}")
            except (json.JSONDecodeError, UnicodeDecodeError):
                raise WorldHTTPError(f"HTTP {e.code}")
        except urllib.error.URLError as e:
            raise WorldHTTPError(f"network: {e}")
        except (json.JSONDecodeError, UnicodeDecodeError) as e:
            raise WorldHTTPError(f"malformed response: {e}")

    def _post(self, path: str, body: Dict) -> Dict:
        url = f"{self.base_url}{path}"
        data = json.dumps(body).encode()
        req = urllib.request.Request(
            url, data=data,
            headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
            method="POST",
        )
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(
                    req, timeout=self.timeout) as r:
                return json.loads(r.read().decode())
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
            try:
                body = json.loads(e.read().decode())
                raise WorldHTTPError(
                    f"HTTP {e.code}: "
                    f"{body.get('error', 'unknown')}")
            except (json.JSONDecodeError, UnicodeDecodeError):
                raise WorldHTTPError(f"HTTP {e.code}")
        except urllib.error.URLError as e:
            raise WorldHTTPError(f"network: {e}")
        except (json.JSONDecodeError, UnicodeDecodeError) as e:
            raise WorldHTTPError(f"malformed response: {e}")

    def manifest(self) -> Dict:
        return self._get("/manifest")

    def petition(self, payload: Dict) -> Dict:
        return self._post("/petition", payload)

    def act(self, payload: Dict) -> Dict:
        return self._post("/act", payload)

    def log(self, since: Optional[str] = None) -> Dict:
        path = "/log"
        if since:
            path += f"?since={urllib.parse.quote(since)}"
        return self._get(path)


# =====================================================================
# Result types
# =====================================================================

@dataclass
class ConnectResult:
    ok: bool
    reason: str
    anchors: Optional[PinnedAnchors] = None

    def format(self) -> str:
        if self.ok:
            return (f"Connected to federation "
                    f"(root {self.anchors.root_fingerprint[:16]}..., "
                    f"{len(self.anchors.world_ids())} worlds)")
        return f"Connection failed: {self.reason}"


@dataclass
class EnterResult:
    ok: bool
    reason: str
    world_id: str = ""
    verified: bool = False
    raw_response: Dict = field(default_factory=dict)


@dataclass
class SubmitResult:
    ok: bool
    reason: str
    world_id: str = ""
    verified: bool = False
    raw_response: Dict = field(default_factory=dict)


# =====================================================================
# ClientState
# =====================================================================

class ClientState:
    """The client's persistent state."""

    IDENTITY_FILE = "identity.json"
    ANCHORS_FILE = "anchors.json"
    PASSPORT_FILE = "passport.json"
    CONTRACTS_FILE = "contracts.json"
    LOG_FILE = "log.jsonl"

    def __init__(self, state_dir: Path):
        self.state_dir = Path(state_dir)
        self.identity: Optional[ClientIdentity] = None
        self.anchors: Optional[PinnedAnchors] = None
        self.passport: Optional[PassportV2] = None
        self.contracts: Dict[str, Dict] = {}
        self._log_buffer: List[Dict] = []

    def exists(self) -> bool:
        return self.state_dir.exists() and any(
            self.state_dir.iterdir())

    def ensure_dir(self) -> None:
        self.state_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    def load(self) -> bool:
        """Load all state files. Returns True iff identity loaded."""
        if not self.state_dir.exists():
            return False
        p = self.state_dir / self.IDENTITY_FILE
        if p.exists():
            self.identity = ClientIdentity.from_dict(
                json.loads(p.read_text()))
        p = self.state_dir / self.ANCHORS_FILE
        if p.exists():
            self.anchors = PinnedAnchors.from_dict(
                json.loads(p.read_text()))
        p = self.state_dir / self.PASSPORT_FILE
        if p.exists():
            self.passport = passport_v2_from_dict(
                json.loads(p.read_text()))
        p = self.state_dir / self.CONTRACTS_FILE
        if p.exists():
            self.contracts = json.loads(p.read_text())
        p = self.state_dir / self.LOG_FILE
        if p.exists():
            # Not loaded into memory; append-only on disk
            pass
        return self.identity is not None

    def save_identity(self) -> None:
        if self.identity is None:
            return
        self.ensure_dir()
        (self.state_dir / self.IDENTITY_FILE).write_text(
            json.dumps(self.identity.to_dict(), indent=2))

    def save_anchors(self) -> None:
        if self.anchors is None:
            return
        self.ensure_dir()
        (self.state_dir / self.ANCHORS_FILE).write_text(
            json.dumps(self.anchors.to_dict(), indent=2))

    def save_passport(self) -> None:
        if self.passport is None:
            return
        self.ensure_dir()
        (self.state_dir / self.PASSPORT_FILE).write_text(
            json.dumps(passport_v2_to_dict(self.passport),
                       indent=2))

    def save_contracts(self) -> None:
        self.ensure_dir()
        (self.state_dir / self.CONTRACTS_FILE).write_text(
            json.dumps(self.contracts, indent=2))

    def append_log(self, kind: str, data: Dict) -> None:
        self.ensure_dir()
        entry = {
            "timestamp": _now(),
            "kind": kind,
            "identity_token":
                self.identity.identity.token
                if self.identity else None,
            "data": data,
        }
        with open(self.state_dir / self.LOG_FILE, "a") as f:
            f.write(json.dumps(entry) + "\n")
        self._log_buffer.append(entry)

    def get_log(self) -> List[Dict]:
        entries = []
        p = self.state_dir / self.LOG_FILE
        if not p.exists():
            return list(self._log_buffer)
        with open(p) as f:
            for line in f:
                line = line.strip()
                if not line:
                    continue
                try:
                    entries.append(json.loads(line))
                except json.JSONDecodeError:
                    continue
        return entries


# =====================================================================
# FederationReport
# =====================================================================

@dataclass
class FederationReport:
    """A signed, self-contained record of a client's activity.

    Includes:
      - The client's identity (token, name, public key)
      - The pinned anchors
      - Every admission the client received (signed by world)
      - Every ack the client received (signed by world)
      - Every refusal (fact, not signed)
      - Contracts the client knows about
      - Generated at (timestamp)
      - Client signature over all of the above
    """
    identity_token: str
    identity_name: str
    identity_public_key: str
    anchors: Dict
    admissions: List[Dict] = field(default_factory=list)
    acks: List[Dict] = field(default_factory=list)
    refusals: List[Dict] = field(default_factory=list)
    contracts: List[Dict] = field(default_factory=list)
    generated_at: str = ""
    client_signature: str = ""

    def canonical_payload(self) -> bytes:
        """The bytes the client signs. Excludes client_signature."""
        return canonical_bytes({
            "kind": "federation_report",
            "identity_token": self.identity_token,
            "identity_name": self.identity_name,
            "identity_public_key": self.identity_public_key,
            "anchors": self.anchors,
            "admissions": self.admissions,
            "acks": self.acks,
            "refusals": self.refusals,
            "contracts": self.contracts,
            "generated_at": self.generated_at,
        })

    def to_dict(self) -> Dict:
        d = json.loads(self.canonical_payload().decode())
        d["client_signature"] = self.client_signature
        return d

    @classmethod
    def from_dict(cls, d: Dict) -> "FederationReport":
        return cls(
            identity_token=d["identity_token"],
            identity_name=d["identity_name"],
            identity_public_key=d["identity_public_key"],
            anchors=d["anchors"],
            admissions=list(d.get("admissions", [])),
            acks=list(d.get("acks", [])),
            refusals=list(d.get("refusals", [])),
            contracts=list(d.get("contracts", [])),
            generated_at=d.get("generated_at", ""),
            client_signature=d.get("client_signature", ""),
        )

    def save(self, path: Path) -> None:
        Path(path).write_text(json.dumps(self.to_dict(), indent=2))

    @classmethod
    def load(cls, path: Path) -> "FederationReport":
        return cls.from_dict(json.loads(Path(path).read_text()))


@dataclass
class ReportVerdict:
    valid: bool
    reason: str
    checks: Dict[str, bool] = field(default_factory=dict)
    errors: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)

    def format(self) -> str:
        lines = ["Report Verification", "=" * 50]
        for name, ok in self.checks.items():
            lines.append(f"  {'✓' if ok else '✗'} {name}")
        for err in self.errors:
            lines.append(f"  ! {err}")
        lines.append("")
        lines.append(
            f"  Result: {'✓ VALID' if self.valid else '✗ INVALID'}")
        if not self.valid:
            lines.append(f"  Reason: {self.reason}")
        return "\n".join(lines)


def verify_report(
    report: FederationReport,
    root_public_key: str,
) -> ReportVerdict:
    """Verify a FederationReport offline.

    A third party supplies the report file and the root public
    key (out of band). The report is self-contained: all
    signatures verify against the anchors embedded in it, and
    the anchors' signature verifies against the root key.

    Never raises.
    """
    if not HAS_CRYPTO:
        return ReportVerdict(
            valid=False, reason="cryptography not installed")
    if not isinstance(report, FederationReport):
        return ReportVerdict(
            valid=False, reason="not a FederationReport")

    checks: Dict[str, bool] = {}
    errors: List[str] = []

    # 1. Anchors signature
    anchors_ok = _verify_anchors_signature(
        report.anchors, root_public_key)
    checks["anchors_signature"] = anchors_ok
    if not anchors_ok:
        errors.append(
            "anchors signature does not verify against root key")

    # Helper: look up a world's public key from anchors
    def _world_key(world_id: str) -> Optional[str]:
        for w in report.anchors.get("worlds", []):
            if w.get("entity_id") == world_id:
                return w.get("curator_public_key")
        return None

    # 2. Client signature
    try:
        client_sig_ok = verify_signature(
            report.identity_public_key,
            report.canonical_payload(),
            report.client_signature)
    except Exception:
        client_sig_ok = False
    checks["client_signature"] = client_sig_ok
    if not client_sig_ok:
        errors.append("client signature does not verify")

    # 3. Admissions
    admission_ok = True
    for i, adm in enumerate(report.admissions):
        world_id = adm.get("entity_id")
        world_key = _world_key(world_id or "")
        if world_key is None:
            admission_ok = False
            errors.append(
                f"admission {i}: world {world_id!r} "
                f"not in anchors")
            continue
        # Reconstruct admission's canonical bytes
        try:
            payload = canonical_bytes({
                "kind": "admission",
                "entity_id": adm["entity_id"],
                "timestamp": adm["timestamp"],
                "subject_token": adm["subject_token"],
            })
            ok = verify_signature(
                world_key, payload, adm.get("signature", ""))
        except Exception as e:
            ok = False
            errors.append(f"admission {i}: {e}")
        if not ok:
            admission_ok = False
            errors.append(
                f"admission {i}: signature INVALID")
        # Subject matches client
        if adm.get("subject_token") != report.identity_token:
            admission_ok = False
            errors.append(
                f"admission {i}: subject_token does not "
                f"match report's client")
    checks["admissions"] = admission_ok

    # 4. Acks
    ack_ok = True
    for i, ack in enumerate(report.acks):
        world_id = ack.get("entity_id")
        world_key = _world_key(world_id or "")
        if world_key is None:
            ack_ok = False
            errors.append(
                f"ack {i}: world {world_id!r} not in anchors")
            continue
        try:
            payload = canonical_bytes({
                "kind": "ack",
                "entity_id": ack["entity_id"],
                "timestamp": ack["timestamp"],
                "subject_token": ack["subject_token"],
            })
            ok = verify_signature(
                world_key, payload, ack.get("signature", ""))
        except Exception as e:
            ok = False
            errors.append(f"ack {i}: {e}")
        if not ok:
            ack_ok = False
            errors.append(f"ack {i}: signature INVALID")
        if ack.get("subject_token") != report.identity_token:
            ack_ok = False
            errors.append(
                f"ack {i}: subject_token does not match")
    checks["acks"] = ack_ok

    # 5. Contracts
    contract_ok = True
    for i, contract in enumerate(report.contracts):
        offer = contract.get("offer", {})
        acceptance = contract.get("acceptance", {})
        proposer_key = _world_key(
            offer.get("proposer_world_id", ""))
        acceptor_key = _world_key(
            acceptance.get("acceptor_world_id", ""))
        if proposer_key is None:
            contract_ok = False
            errors.append(
                f"contract {i}: proposer world not in anchors")
        else:
            try:
                offer_payload = canonical_bytes({
                    "kind": "contract_offer",
                    "proposer_world_id":
                        offer["proposer_world_id"],
                    "proposer_public_key":
                        offer["proposer_public_key"],
                    "target_world_id": offer["target_world_id"],
                    "terms": offer["terms"],
                    "timestamp": offer["timestamp"],
                })
                ok = verify_signature(
                    proposer_key, offer_payload,
                    offer.get("signature", ""))
            except Exception:
                ok = False
            if not ok:
                contract_ok = False
                errors.append(
                    f"contract {i}: offer sig INVALID")
        if acceptor_key is None:
            contract_ok = False
            errors.append(
                f"contract {i}: acceptor world not in anchors")
        else:
            try:
                acc_payload = canonical_bytes({
                    "kind": "contract_acceptance",
                    "acceptor_world_id":
                        acceptance["acceptor_world_id"],
                    "acceptor_public_key":
                        acceptance["acceptor_public_key"],
                    "offer_hash": acceptance["offer_hash"],
                    "terms_hash": acceptance["terms_hash"],
                    "timestamp": acceptance["timestamp"],
                })
                ok = verify_signature(
                    acceptor_key, acc_payload,
                    acceptance.get("signature", ""))
            except Exception:
                ok = False
            if not ok:
                contract_ok = False
                errors.append(
                    f"contract {i}: acceptance sig INVALID")
    checks["contracts"] = contract_ok

    all_ok = all(checks.values())
    if all_ok:
        reason = "all checks passed"
    else:
        failed = [k for k, v in checks.items() if not v]
        reason = "failed: " + ", ".join(failed)
    return ReportVerdict(
        valid=all_ok, reason=reason,
        checks=checks, errors=errors)


# =====================================================================
# FederationClient
# =====================================================================

class FederationClient:
    """The main client. Holds state, orchestrates operations."""

    def __init__(self, state_dir: Path):
        if not HAS_CRYPTO:
            raise RuntimeError(
                "FederationClient requires `cryptography`")
        self.state = ClientState(state_dir)

    # -- Setup ---------------------------------------------------

    def create_identity(self, name: str) -> ClientIdentity:
        """Generate a new identity and persist it."""
        ident = create_identity(name)
        kp = KeyPair.generate()
        client_identity = ClientIdentity(
            identity=ident, keypair=kp)
        self.state.identity = client_identity
        self.state.passport = PassportV2.new(ident)
        self.state.save_identity()
        self.state.save_passport()
        self.state.append_log(
            "identity_created",
            {"token": ident.token, "name": name})
        return client_identity

    def load_state(self) -> bool:
        return self.state.load()

    def connect(
        self, anchor_url: str, root_public_key: str,
    ) -> ConnectResult:
        """Fetch, verify, and pin the federation anchors."""
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(
                    anchor_url, timeout=10.0) as r:
                raw = json.loads(r.read().decode())
        except urllib.error.URLError as e:
            return ConnectResult(
                ok=False, reason=f"network: {e}")
        except (json.JSONDecodeError, UnicodeDecodeError) as e:
            return ConnectResult(
                ok=False, reason=f"malformed anchors: {e}")
        if raw.get("kind") != "federation_trust_anchors":
            return ConnectResult(
                ok=False,
                reason=f"wrong kind {raw.get('kind')!r}")
        if not _verify_anchors_signature(raw, root_public_key):
            return ConnectResult(
                ok=False,
                reason="anchors signature invalid")
        if not isinstance(raw.get("worlds"), list) \
                or not raw["worlds"]:
            return ConnectResult(
                ok=False, reason="anchors have no worlds")
        pinned = PinnedAnchors(
            anchor_url=anchor_url,
            root_fingerprint=root_public_key,
            raw=raw,
            fetched_at=_now(),
        )
        self.state.anchors = pinned
        self.state.save_anchors()
        self.state.append_log(
            "anchors_pinned",
            {"anchor_url": anchor_url,
             "root_fingerprint": root_public_key,
             "world_ids": pinned.world_ids()})
        return ConnectResult(ok=True, reason="connected",
                              anchors=pinned)

    # -- World entry ---------------------------------------------

    def _world_http(
        self, world_id: str,
    ) -> Tuple[Optional[WorldHTTPClient], Optional[str]]:
        """Look up the world's base URL from anchors and return
        an HTTP client, or a reason string if not found."""
        if self.state.anchors is None:
            return (None, "not connected to a federation")
        base_url = self.state.anchors.world_base_url(world_id)
        if base_url is None:
            return (None, f"world {world_id!r} not in anchors")
        return (WorldHTTPClient(base_url), None)

    def _verify_manifest_matches_anchors(
        self, world_id: str, manifest: Dict,
    ) -> Tuple[bool, str]:
        """Verify a fetched manifest matches the anchors.

        If the manifest is a C28 SignedManifest (has signature,
        signed_by, public_key), verify its signature against the
        anchors' curator key. Otherwise, require the manifest's
        entity_id to match; rely on HTTPS for integrity.
        """
        if manifest.get("entity_id") != world_id:
            return (False,
                    f"manifest entity_id "
                    f"{manifest.get('entity_id')!r} != "
                    f"{world_id!r}")
        has_sig = (
            isinstance(manifest.get("signature"), str)
            and manifest.get("signature"))
        if has_sig:
            world_key = self.state.anchors.world_public_key(world_id)
            if world_key is None:
                return (False, "world not in anchors")
            # C28 signed manifest canonical payload
            body = {k: v for k, v in manifest.items()
                    if k != "signature"}
            try:
                ok = verify_signature(
                    world_key, canonical_bytes(body),
                    manifest["signature"])
            except Exception:
                ok = False
            if not ok:
                return (False, "manifest signature INVALID")
        return (True, "manifest matches anchors")

    def _verify_admission(
        self, response: Dict, world_id: str,
    ) -> Tuple[bool, str]:
        """Verify a signed admission against the anchors."""
        world_key = self.state.anchors.world_public_key(world_id)
        if world_key is None:
            return (False, "world not in anchors")
        if response.get("kind") != "admission":
            return (False,
                    f"response kind "
                    f"{response.get('kind')!r} is not admission")
        try:
            payload = canonical_bytes({
                "kind": "admission",
                "entity_id": response["entity_id"],
                "timestamp": response["timestamp"],
                "subject_token": response["subject_token"],
            })
            ok = verify_signature(
                world_key, payload,
                response.get("signature", ""))
        except (KeyError, TypeError) as e:
            return (False, f"malformed admission: {e}")
        except Exception:
            ok = False
        if not ok:
            return (False, "signature INVALID")
        return (True, "admission verified")

    def _verify_ack(
        self, response: Dict, world_id: str,
    ) -> Tuple[bool, str]:
        world_key = self.state.anchors.world_public_key(world_id)
        if world_key is None:
            return (False, "world not in anchors")
        if response.get("kind") != "ack":
            return (False,
                    f"response kind "
                    f"{response.get('kind')!r} is not ack")
        try:
            payload = canonical_bytes({
                "kind": "ack",
                "entity_id": response["entity_id"],
                "timestamp": response["timestamp"],
                "subject_token": response["subject_token"],
            })
            ok = verify_signature(
                world_key, payload,
                response.get("signature", ""))
        except (KeyError, TypeError) as e:
            return (False, f"malformed ack: {e}")
        except Exception:
            ok = False
        if not ok:
            return (False, "signature INVALID")
        return (True, "ack verified")

    def enter_world(self, world_id: str) -> EnterResult:
        """Petition a world. Verify the response. Update passport."""
        if self.state.identity is None:
            return EnterResult(
                ok=False, reason="no identity; run `create_identity` first")
        if self.state.anchors is None:
            return EnterResult(
                ok=False, reason="not connected to a federation")
        client, err = self._world_http(world_id)
        if client is None:
            return EnterResult(ok=False, reason=err or "unknown")
        # Fetch manifest
        try:
            manifest = client.manifest()
        except WorldHTTPError as e:
            return EnterResult(
                ok=False, reason=f"manifest fetch: {e}")
        ok, reason = self._verify_manifest_matches_anchors(
            world_id, manifest)
        if not ok:
            return EnterResult(ok=False, reason=reason)
        # Send petition
        passport_admissions = list(
            self.state.passport.to_plain_entries())
        try:
            response = client.petition({
                "petitioner_token": self.state.identity.identity.token,
                "petitioner_name": self.state.identity.identity.name,
                "passport_admissions": passport_admissions,
                "message": "client entry",
            })
        except WorldHTTPError as e:
            return EnterResult(
                ok=False, reason=f"petition failed: {e}")
        if response.get("kind") == "admission":
            ok, vreason = self._verify_admission(response, world_id)
            if ok:
                entry = PassportEntry(
                    entity_id=response["entity_id"],
                    timestamp=response["timestamp"],
                    subject_token=response["subject_token"],
                    signature=response["signature"],
                )
                self.state.passport = self.state.passport.with_entry(entry)
                self.state.save_passport()
            self.state.append_log(
                "enter_world",
                {"world_id": world_id,
                 "ok": True, "verified": ok,
                 "reason": vreason,
                 "admission": response})
            return EnterResult(
                ok=True, reason=vreason,
                world_id=world_id, verified=ok,
                raw_response=response)
        elif response.get("kind") == "refusal":
            self.state.append_log(
                "enter_world",
                {"world_id": world_id, "ok": False,
                 "refused": True,
                 "reason": response.get("reason", "")})
            return EnterResult(
                ok=False,
                reason=f"refused: {response.get('reason', '')}",
                world_id=world_id, raw_response=response)
        else:
            return EnterResult(
                ok=False,
                reason=f"unexpected response: {response.get('kind')}",
                world_id=world_id, raw_response=response)

    def submit_act(
        self,
        world_id: str,
        act_type: str,
        payload: Dict,
    ) -> SubmitResult:
        if self.state.identity is None:
            return SubmitResult(
                ok=False, reason="no identity")
        client, err = self._world_http(world_id)
        if client is None:
            return SubmitResult(ok=False, reason=err or "unknown")
        try:
            response = client.act({
                "actor_token": self.state.identity.identity.token,
                "type": act_type,
                "payload": payload,
            })
        except WorldHTTPError as e:
            return SubmitResult(
                ok=False, reason=f"act failed: {e}")
        if response.get("kind") == "ack":
            ok, vreason = self._verify_ack(response, world_id)
            self.state.append_log(
                "submit_act",
                {"world_id": world_id,
                 "act_type": act_type,
                 "ok": True, "verified": ok,
                 "reason": vreason,
                 "response": response,
                 "payload": payload})
            return SubmitResult(
                ok=True, reason=vreason,
                world_id=world_id, verified=ok,
                raw_response=response)
        elif response.get("kind") == "refusal":
            self.state.append_log(
                "submit_act",
                {"world_id": world_id,
                 "act_type": act_type,
                 "ok": False, "refused": True,
                 "reason": response.get("reason", ""),
                 "payload": payload})
            return SubmitResult(
                ok=False,
                reason=f"refused: {response.get('reason', '')}",
                world_id=world_id, raw_response=response)
        else:
            return SubmitResult(
                ok=False,
                reason=f"unexpected response: {response.get('kind')}",
                world_id=world_id, raw_response=response)

    def cite_contract(
        self,
        world_id: str,
        contract_id: str,
        cites_world: str,
        act_type: str = "poem.turn",
        base_payload: Optional[Dict] = None,
    ) -> SubmitResult:
        payload = dict(base_payload or {})
        payload["cites_contract"] = contract_id
        payload["cites_world"] = cites_world
        return self.submit_act(world_id, act_type, payload)

    # -- Verification --------------------------------------------

    def verify_state(self) -> ReportVerdict:
        """Verify everything the client holds, offline."""
        if self.state.identity is None:
            return ReportVerdict(
                valid=False, reason="no identity")
        if self.state.anchors is None:
            return ReportVerdict(
                valid=False, reason="no anchors pinned")
        # Build a report and verify it
        report = self.build_report()
        verdict = verify_report(
            report, self.state.anchors.root_fingerprint)
        self.state.append_log(
            "verify_state",
            {"valid": verdict.valid, "reason": verdict.reason})
        return verdict

    # -- Report --------------------------------------------------

    def build_report(self) -> FederationReport:
        """Produce a signed, self-contained federation report."""
        if self.state.identity is None:
            raise RuntimeError("no identity")
        if self.state.anchors is None:
            raise RuntimeError("no anchors pinned")
        # Split log entries by kind
        admissions: List[Dict] = []
        acks: List[Dict] = []
        refusals: List[Dict] = []
        for entry in self.state.get_log():
            if entry.get("kind") == "enter_world":
                data = entry.get("data", {})
                if data.get("ok") and data.get("admission"):
                    admissions.append(data["admission"])
                elif data.get("refused"):
                    refusals.append({
                        "world_id": data.get("world_id"),
                        "reason": data.get("reason", ""),
                    })
            elif entry.get("kind") == "submit_act":
                data = entry.get("data", {})
                if data.get("ok") and data.get("response"):
                    acks.append(data["response"])
                elif data.get("refused"):
                    refusals.append({
                        "world_id": data.get("world_id"),
                        "act_type": data.get("act_type"),
                        "reason": data.get("reason", ""),
                    })
        # Contracts from state
        contracts = list(self.state.contracts.values())
        generated_at = _now()
        report = FederationReport(
            identity_token=self.state.identity.identity.token,
            identity_name=self.state.identity.identity.name,
            identity_public_key=(
                self.state.identity.keypair.public_key_hex()),
            anchors=self.state.anchors.raw,
            admissions=admissions,
            acks=acks,
            refusals=refusals,
            contracts=contracts,
            generated_at=generated_at,
            client_signature="",  # placeholder
        )
        # Sign
        signature = self.state.identity.keypair.sign(
            report.canonical_payload()).hex()
        report.client_signature = signature
        return report


# =====================================================================
# CLI
# =====================================================================

DEFAULT_STATE_DIR = Path.home() / ".lfs"


def _format_state_summary(client: FederationClient) -> str:
    lines = []
    if client.state.identity is None:
        lines.append("No identity yet.")
        return "\n".join(lines)
    ident = client.state.identity
    lines.append(
        f"Identity:  {ident.identity.name} "
        f"({ident.identity.token[:16]}...)")
    if client.state.anchors is not None:
        a = client.state.anchors
        lines.append(
            f"Anchors:   {a.root_fingerprint[:16]}... "
            f"({len(a.world_ids())} worlds)")
        lines.append(f"Worlds:    {', '.join(a.world_ids())}")
    else:
        lines.append("Anchors:   (not connected)")
    if client.state.passport is not None:
        n = len(client.state.passport)
        lines.append(f"Passport:  {n} entries")
    else:
        lines.append("Passport:  (none)")
    lines.append(f"Contracts: {len(client.state.contracts)}")
    log = client.state.get_log()
    lines.append(f"Log:       {len(log)} entries")
    return "\n".join(lines)


def _cmd_init(client: FederationClient, args) -> int:
    if client.state.exists():
        print(f"State already exists at {client.state.state_dir}",
              file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    ident = client.create_identity(args.name)
    print(f"Created identity: {ident.identity.name}")
    print(f"  token:      {ident.identity.token}")
    print(f"  public key: {ident.keypair.public_key_hex()}")
    print(f"  state:      {client.state.state_dir}")
    return 0


def _cmd_connect(client: FederationClient, args) -> int:
    if not client.load_state() or client.state.identity is None:
        print("No identity; run `init <name>` first",
              file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    result = client.connect(args.anchor_url, args.root_key)
    print(result.format())
    return 0 if result.ok else 1


def _cmd_status(client: FederationClient, args) -> int:
    if not client.load_state() or client.state.identity is None:
        print("No identity; run `init <name>` first",
              file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    print(_format_state_summary(client))
    return 0


def _cmd_enter(client: FederationClient, args) -> int:
    if not client.load_state() or client.state.identity is None:
        print("No identity", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    result = client.enter_world(args.world_id)
    if result.ok:
        print(f"Entered {result.world_id}")
        print(f"  verified: {result.verified}")
        print(f"  reason:   {result.reason}")
        return 0
    print(f"Enter failed: {result.reason}", file=sys.stderr)
    return 1


def _cmd_act(client: FederationClient, args) -> int:
    if not client.load_state() or client.state.identity is None:
        print("No identity", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    try:
        payload = json.loads(args.payload_json)
    except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
        print(f"Invalid payload JSON: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    result = client.submit_act(args.world_id, args.act_type, payload)
    if result.ok:
        print(f"Act accepted by {result.world_id}")
        print(f"  verified: {result.verified}")
        return 0
    print(f"Act failed: {result.reason}", file=sys.stderr)
    return 1


def _cmd_cite(client: FederationClient, args) -> int:
    if not client.load_state() or client.state.identity is None:
        print("No identity", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    result = client.cite_contract(
        args.world_id, args.contract_id, args.cites_world)
    if result.ok:
        print(f"Citation accepted by {result.world_id}")
        return 0
    print(f"Citation failed: {result.reason}", file=sys.stderr)
    return 1


def _cmd_verify(client: FederationClient, args) -> int:
    if not client.load_state() or client.state.identity is None:
        print("No identity", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    verdict = client.verify_state()
    print(verdict.format())
    return 0 if verdict.valid else 1


def _cmd_report(client: FederationClient, args) -> int:
    if not client.load_state() or client.state.identity is None:
        print("No identity", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    report = client.build_report()
    if args.output:
        path = Path(args.output)
    else:
        path = client.state.state_dir / "report.json"
    report.save(path)
    print(f"Report written to {path}")
    print(f"  identity:  {report.identity_name}")
    print(f"  admissions: {len(report.admissions)}")
    print(f"  acks:       {len(report.acks)}")
    print(f"  contracts:  {len(report.contracts)}")
    return 0


def _cmd_verify_report(client: FederationClient, args) -> int:
    try:
        report = FederationReport.load(Path(args.report_path))
    except (FileNotFoundError, json.JSONDecodeError) as e:
        print(f"Could not load report: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    verdict = verify_report(report, args.root_key)
    print(verdict.format())
    return 0 if verdict.valid else 1


def main(argv: Optional[List[str]] = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="lfs",
        description="The LFS/0.1 reference client.",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--state-dir", default=str(DEFAULT_STATE_DIR),
        help="State directory (default: ~/.lfs)")
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)

    p = sub.add_parser("init", help="Create a new identity")
    p.add_argument("name", help="Display name")
    p.set_defaults(func=_cmd_init)

    p = sub.add_parser("connect", help="Pin federation anchors")
    p.add_argument("anchor_url", help="Anchors file URL")
    p.add_argument("root_key", help="Root public key (hex)")
    p.set_defaults(func=_cmd_connect)

    p = sub.add_parser("status", help="Show state summary")
    p.set_defaults(func=_cmd_status)

    p = sub.add_parser("enter", help="Petition a world")
    p.add_argument("world_id")
    p.set_defaults(func=_cmd_enter)

    p = sub.add_parser("act", help="Submit an act")
    p.add_argument("world_id")
    p.add_argument("act_type")
    p.add_argument("payload_json")
    p.set_defaults(func=_cmd_act)

    p = sub.add_parser("cite", help="Cite a contract in an act")
    p.add_argument("world_id")
    p.add_argument("contract_id")
    p.add_argument("cites_world")
    p.set_defaults(func=_cmd_cite)

    p = sub.add_parser("verify", help="Verify all state")
    p.set_defaults(func=_cmd_verify)

    p = sub.add_parser("report", help="Build and save a report")
    p.add_argument("--output", default=None)
    p.set_defaults(func=_cmd_report)

    p = sub.add_parser(
        "verify-report", help="Verify an external report")
    p.add_argument("report_path")
    p.add_argument("root_key")
    p.set_defaults(func=_cmd_verify_report)

    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    client = FederationClient(Path(args.state_dir))
    try:
        return args.func(client, args)
    except RuntimeError as e:
        print(f"Error: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1


# =====================================================================
# Demo
# =====================================================================

def demo(artifact_dir: Optional[str] = None) -> Dict:
    """Client against two signed worlds over HTTP.

    1. Spin up Poetry World and Chemistry World (signed, C13).
    2. Build anchors (signed by a root key).
    3. Client: create identity, connect, enter both worlds,
       submit acts, verify state, produce report.
    4. "Third-party verifier": loads report + root key, verifies
       offline, in a fresh process.
    """
    import json as _json
    from pathlib import Path
    from multiverse_c3 import Act, Ack
    from multiverse_c4 import PoetryWorld
    from multiverse_c5 import ChemistryWorld
    from multiverse_c13 import SignedWorld
    from wcp_http_shim import WorldProtocolServer

    if not HAS_CRYPTO:
        raise RuntimeError("demo requires `cryptography`")

    if artifact_dir is None:
        artifact_dir = "artifacts"
    path = Path(artifact_dir)
    path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    # -- Two signed worlds ----------------------------------------
    poetry_kp = KeyPair.generate()
    poetry = SignedWorld(
        PoetryWorld("world:poetry", "Poetry"), poetry_kp)
    poetry_srv = WorldProtocolServer(poetry, port=0)
    poetry_srv.serve_in_thread()
    chemistry_kp = KeyPair.generate()
```
