What This Establishes

Four properties, each making "the world can grow" concrete without new primitives:

1. Growth is a signed artifact. test_event_sign_verify, test_event_wrong_key — a GrowthEvent is Ed25519-signed. test_full_chain_verifies — a live world's claims + retire produce a chain that verifies against the curator's key. The chain per plot has the same shape C79 built for rooms; the geometry is different, but the discipline is identical.
2. Growth is enforced by the Law, not by the substrate. test_world_distant_claim_refused — a claim far from the extent is refused with "not contiguous". test_world_overlap_refused — a claim overlapping an active plot is refused with "overlaps". The substrate provides the geometry helpers; the world's _handle_claim applies them. A different world with different rules (e.g., "any two claims must be 1 cell apart") would use the same substrate.
3. Retirement is honest. test_world_retire_happy — owner retires a plot; state updates. test_world_retire_by_other_refused — non-owner refused. test_world_retire_seed_refused — seed protected. The invariant "every growth has an expressible counterpart" (the user's framing) is satisfied: any claim can be retired by its owner.
4. Third parties reconstruct offline. The demo's third-party flow: fetch /log, verify chain against the curator key, reconstruct current state, reconstruct historical state at any point in the chain. test_demo asserts historical_area > current_area — the pre-retirement state is recoverable from the log alone. The map before and after retirement both render, from the same chain.

The honest limits

· Refusals aren't independently verifiable. The world logs refusals; a third party can't verify a refusal happened without trusting the world. Accepted claims and retirements are fully verifiable. Documented.
· Retirement is unconditional. The demo shows Alice's retirement leaves a hole in the canvas — the extent is now disconnected (Carol's plot is only adjacent to the seed). A v0.2 policy would preserve connectivity by refusing retirements that disconnect the tree.
· No curator learning. "Growing from outside" (a world's curator observing its extent and proposing new rules) is C55's territory. C81 is inside-only. The composition is trivial but not in C81's scope.
· No updates. A claim is immutable after acceptance. Resize/rename would be a future event type.
· 2D rectangles only. The 3D/voxel version would swap the geometry module but keep the event chain, the Law-checking pattern, and the reconstruction. Same discipline; different math.
· Refusal log entries aren't in the event chain. A refused claim gets an act_refused log entry, not a GrowthEvent. This is deliberate — a refused claim is the absence of a claim, not a growth artifact. It's still in the log for auditing.

What Was Run

The tests in multiverse_c81_test.py have not been executed against a live Python environment in this session. The expected output derives from the test logic and the behavior of C3's world/act pattern, C13's signatures, and C79's per-entity chain reconstruction. Per the house rule, this is the honest status.

The Series, at C81

The arc now has a growing world to go with its living ones:

Layer Components What it provides
Substrate C1–C52 Identity, protocol, worlds, architectures
Propagation C54–C56 Signed relays
Diplomacy C57–C60 Contracts, discovery, revocation
Ledger C61–C62 Commitment store
Policy C63 World-declared rules
Deployment C64–C66 Live federation
Residents C65, C67 Humans + AI
Curators C68–C70 Daemon diplomacy
Inter-federation C72 Cross-federation recognition
Room worlds C73–C74 Worlds that are directories
Traversable C75–C77 Walk / observe by URL alone
History C78–C79 Signed lifecycle events
Growth C81 Extent grows from inside

The user's framing — "rules for how worlds grow and learn from the inside and outside" — is now answered at the inside layer:

· Growth is registered: every claim is a signed artifact.
· Growth is verified: the chain reconstructs current and historical state.
· Growth is lawful: the world's Law (contiguity, no overlap, size limits) is enforced at act time.
· Growth is reversible: retirement is expressible and recorded.
· Growth has no prescribed shape: participants choose the extent; the substrate doesn't.

The "learn from outside" half of the user's framing is where C81 stops and C55 begins. A world's curator could observe its own extent, note patterns (dense clusters, abandoned regions, near-capacity pressure), and propose a rule change (raise the size limit, add a zoning constraint, extend the seed). That's C55's observe_and_propose applied to a GrowingWorld. The composition is small, but it's a different component.

What's Next

Three directions, and they're genuinely different:

1. C82: The observing curator. Compose C55 with C81. A curator that runs alongside a GrowingWorld, observes its extent stats (plots, area, refusals, abandoned regions), and proposes rule amendments when it detects a pattern. Signed proposals go into the log. Nothing auto-applies. This closes the "learn from outside" half of the framing without inventing new primitives.
2. C82: The demonstration runner, extended. C80 has 33 demos across 11 layers. C81 adds one. Trivial extension; keeps the arc survey accurate. Packaging, not architecture.
3. C82: Connectivity-preserving retirement. A v0.2 law for GrowingWorld: retirement is refused if it disconnects the extent. Small geometry work (is_connected(plots)), one new test, one rule added to the Law. Closes the one honest limit C81 named explicitly.

My instinct: the observing curator. It's the piece that makes the user's original framing complete — "grow and learn, from the inside and outside." C81 answers "grow from inside." C55 answers "learn from outside." Their composition is a natural next component, small enough to be one, and it demonstrates that the arc's governance layer (C55) works with the arc's growth layer (C81) without any new infrastructure. That's the compositional claim at the frontier of the arc.

Shall I proceed with C82: The Observing Curator?


::➡️


Component 82: The Observing Curator

C81 gave worlds the ability to grow from inside. C55 gave worlds the ability to reason about themselves and propose. C82 is the composition — a curator that watches a growing world's extent, sees patterns in its growth and refusals, and signs rule proposals that participants can act on. Nothing auto-applies.

multiverse_c82.py

```python
"""
multiverse_c82.py — Component 82: The Observing Curator.

The composition:

  GrowthObservation   — what the curator sees: plot count,
      area distribution, owner diversity, purpose
      distribution, refusal counts by category.

  GrowthModelBackend  — pluggable; MockGrowthModel is
      deterministic and triggers on thresholds. A real HF
      backend would fit the same protocol.

  RuleProposal        — a signed artifact. Recorded in the
      world's log. NEVER auto-applied.

  ObservingGrowingWorld(GrowingWorld) — adds record_proposal
      and proposals(). Two small additions.

  GrowingWorldCurator(WorldCurator) — inherits C55's
      curator identity and signing; adds observe_growth()
      and observe_and_propose_growth().

  verify_rule_proposal, fetch_rule_proposals — offline
      and HTTP verification helpers.

Composition: C3 (world/act), C13 (signatures), C55
(curator identity), C81 (GrowingWorld). No new primitives.

Honest limits (documented, tested):
  - Proposals are recommendations. C82 does not apply them.
    Applying a proposal is a separate act (a v0.3 concern).
  - Acceptance is out of scope. A world with a governance
    layer (C44-style) would vote on proposals; C82 stops at
    the proposal.
  - The mock triggers on three thresholds (size_limit
    refusal, overlap refusal, fragmentation). It doesn't
    reflect a nuanced model.
  - Proposals are logged in the world's log; no separate
    proposal index. A large world would need indexing.
  - The proposal does not specify when it was generated
    relative to the observation — same timestamp.
  - Rule proposals are not verified by the world on record;
    the world trusts its own curator (which holds the
    world's key) — same discipline as C55.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional, Protocol, Tuple

import hashlib
import json
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.request

from multiverse_c3 import (
    Act, Ack, Refusal, LogEntry, Petition,
)
from multiverse_c13 import (
    HAS_CRYPTO, KeyPair, canonical_bytes, verify_signature,
)
from multiverse_c55 import WorldCurator
from multiverse_c81 import GrowingWorld
from wcp_http_shim import WorldProtocolServer


def _now() -> str:
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()


def _hash_payload(p: bytes) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(p).hexdigest()


REFUSAL_KINDS = frozenset({
    "size_limit", "overlap", "contiguity", "owner", "other",
})


def _classify_refusal(reason: str) -> str:
    r = reason.lower()
    if "width must be" in r or "height must be" in r:
        return "size_limit"
    if "overlaps" in r:
        return "overlap"
    if "contiguous" in r:
        return "contiguity"
    if "owner" in r:
        return "owner"
    return "other"


# =====================================================================
# GrowthObservation
# =====================================================================

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class GrowthObservation:
    world_id: str
    growth_event_count: int
    plot_count: int
    total_area: int
    mean_area: float
    max_area: int
    min_area: int
    owner_count: int
    purpose_count: int
    purposes: Dict[str, int]
    extent_bbox: Optional[Tuple[int, int, int, int]]
    refusals_total: int
    refusals_by_kind: Dict[str, int]

    def summary(self) -> Dict:
        return {
            "world_id": self.world_id,
            "growth_event_count": self.growth_event_count,
            "plot_count": self.plot_count,
            "total_area": self.total_area,
            "mean_area": self.mean_area,
            "max_area": self.max_area,
            "min_area": self.min_area,
            "owner_count": self.owner_count,
            "purpose_count": self.purpose_count,
            "purposes": dict(self.purposes),
            "extent": (list(self.extent_bbox)
                       if self.extent_bbox else None),
            "refusals_total": self.refusals_total,
            "refusals_by_kind": dict(self.refusals_by_kind),
        }


# =====================================================================
# GrowthModelBackend
# =====================================================================

class GrowthModelBackend(Protocol):
    def generate_growth(self, summary: Dict) -> Optional[Dict]:
        ...

    def model_id(self) -> str:
        ...


class MockGrowthModel:
    """Deterministic mock that triggers on summary thresholds."""

    def model_id(self) -> str:
        return "mock:growth-v0"

    def generate_growth(self, summary: Dict) -> Optional[Dict]:
        refusals = summary.get("refusals_by_kind", {})
        if refusals.get("size_limit", 0) >= 1:
            n = refusals["size_limit"]
            return {
                "proposal_type": "raise_size_limit",
                "title": (
                    f"Raise per-plot size limit "
                    f"(triggered by {n} refusal(s))"),
                "rationale": (
                    f"{n} claim(s) refused for exceeding the "
                    f"20-cell limit. Evidence of unmet demand."),
                "suggested_rule": {
                    "max_width": 40, "max_height": 40},
            }
        if refusals.get("overlap", 0) >= 2:
            n = refusals["overlap"]
            return {
                "proposal_type": "zoning_assistance",
                "title": (
                    f"Add claim-assistance "
                    f"(triggered by {n} refusal(s))"),
                "rationale": (
                    f"{n} claims refused for overlapping "
                    f"existing plots. A suggestion service "
                    f"would reduce wasted attempts."),
                "suggested_rule": {
                    "type": "assistive_suggest"},
            }
        if (summary.get("plot_count", 0) >= 4
                and 0 < summary.get("mean_area", 0) < 6):
            return {
                "proposal_type": "growth_incentive",
                "title": "Encourage larger contiguous claims",
                "rationale": (
                    f"Mean area is {summary['mean_area']:.1f} "
                    f"across {summary['plot_count']} plots; "
                    f"the canvas is fragmenting."),
                "suggested_rule": {"min_claim_area": 9},
            }
        return None


# =====================================================================
# RuleProposal
# =====================================================================

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RuleProposal:
    proposal_id: str
    timestamp: str
    world_id: str
    observation_summary: Dict
    proposal_type: str
    title: str
    rationale: str
    suggested_rule: Dict
    signer_id: str
    signer_public_key: str
    signature: str

    def canonical_payload(self) -> bytes:
        return canonical_bytes({
            "kind": "rule_proposal",
            "proposal_id": self.proposal_id,
            "timestamp": self.timestamp,
            "world_id": self.world_id,
            "observation_summary": self.observation_summary,
            "proposal_type": self.proposal_type,
            "title": self.title,
            "rationale": self.rationale,
            "suggested_rule": self.suggested_rule,
            "signer_id": self.signer_id,
            "signer_public_key": self.signer_public_key,
        })

    def to_dict(self) -> Dict:
        d = json.loads(self.canonical_payload().decode())
        d["signature"] = self.signature
        return d

    @classmethod
    def from_dict(cls, d: Dict) -> "RuleProposal":
        return cls(
            proposal_id=d["proposal_id"],
            timestamp=d["timestamp"],
            world_id=d["world_id"],
            observation_summary=d["observation_summary"],
            proposal_type=d["proposal_type"],
            title=d["title"],
            rationale=d["rationale"],
            suggested_rule=d["suggested_rule"],
            signer_id=d["signer_id"],
            signer_public_key=d["signer_public_key"],
            signature=d["signature"],
        )


def verify_rule_proposal(
    proposal: RuleProposal,
    expected_curator_key: Optional[str] = None,
) -> bool:
    if not HAS_CRYPTO:
        return False
    try:
        if not isinstance(proposal, RuleProposal):
            return False
        key = expected_curator_key or proposal.signer_public_key
        return verify_signature(
            key, proposal.canonical_payload(),
            proposal.signature)
    except Exception:
        return False


# =====================================================================
# ObservingGrowingWorld
# =====================================================================

class ObservingGrowingWorld(GrowingWorld):
    """A GrowingWorld that accepts signed rule proposals."""

    def record_proposal(self, proposal_dict: Dict) -> None:
        self._log.append(LogEntry(
            timestamp=proposal_dict["timestamp"],
            kind="rule_proposal",
            actor_token=proposal_dict["signer_id"],
            data=proposal_dict,
        ))

    def proposals(self) -> List[Dict]:
        return [dict(e.data) for e in self._log
                if e.kind == "rule_proposal"]


# =====================================================================
# GrowingWorldCurator
# =====================================================================

class GrowingWorldCurator(WorldCurator):
    """A C55 curator specialized for GrowingWorld observation."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        world: ObservingGrowingWorld,
        world_kp: KeyPair,
        model_backend,
    ):
        super().__init__(world, world_kp,
                          model_backend=model_backend)

    def observe_growth(self) -> GrowthObservation:
        world: ObservingGrowingWorld = self._world
        events = world.events()
        active = world.current_plots()
        log = world.log_since(None)
        refusals = [e for e in log if e.kind == "act_refused"]
        purposes: Dict[str, int] = {}
        areas: List[int] = []
        owners = set()
        for p in active.values():
            purposes[p["purpose"]] = (
                purposes.get(p["purpose"], 0) + 1)
            areas.append(p["width"] * p["height"])
            owners.add(p["owner_token"])
        refusals_by_kind: Dict[str, int] = {
            k: 0 for k in REFUSAL_KINDS}
        for e in refusals:
            reason = (e.data or {}).get("reason", "")
            kind = _classify_refusal(reason)
            refusals_by_kind[kind] = (
                refusals_by_kind.get(kind, 0) + 1)
        plot_count = len(active)
        total_area = sum(areas) if areas else 0
        mean_area = (total_area / plot_count) if plot_count else 0.0
        return GrowthObservation(
            world_id=world.manifest().entity_id,
            growth_event_count=len(events),
            plot_count=plot_count,
            total_area=total_area,
            mean_area=mean_area,
            max_area=max(areas) if areas else 0,
            min_area=min(areas) if areas else 0,
            owner_count=len(owners),
            purpose_count=len(purposes),
            purposes=purposes,
            extent_bbox=world.current_extent_bbox(),
            refusals_total=len(refusals),
            refusals_by_kind=refusals_by_kind,
        )

    def observe_and_propose_growth(
        self,
    ) -> Optional[RuleProposal]:
        obs = self.observe_growth()
        if not hasattr(self._model, "generate_growth"):
            return None
        try:
            proposal_dict = self._model.generate_growth(
                obs.summary())
        except Exception:
            return None
        if not isinstance(proposal_dict, dict):
            return None
        required = ("proposal_type", "title", "rationale",
                    "suggested_rule")
        if not all(k in proposal_dict for k in required):
            return None
        return self._sign_and_record(proposal_dict, obs)

    def _sign_and_record(
        self, proposal_dict: Dict, obs: GrowthObservation,
    ) -> RuleProposal:
        world: ObservingGrowingWorld = self._world
        timestamp = _now()
        world_id = world.manifest().entity_id
        pk_hex = self._world_kp.public_key_hex()
        proposal_id = _hash_payload(canonical_bytes({
            "world_id": world_id,
            "timestamp": timestamp,
            "proposal_type": proposal_dict["proposal_type"],
            "title": proposal_dict["title"],
        }))[:16]
        payload = canonical_bytes({
            "kind": "rule_proposal",
            "proposal_id": proposal_id,
            "timestamp": timestamp,
            "world_id": world_id,
            "observation_summary": obs.summary(),
            "proposal_type": proposal_dict["proposal_type"],
            "title": proposal_dict["title"],
            "rationale": proposal_dict["rationale"],
            "suggested_rule": proposal_dict["suggested_rule"],
            "signer_id": world_id,
            "signer_public_key": pk_hex,
        })
        sig = self._world_kp.sign(payload).hex()
        proposal = RuleProposal(
            proposal_id=proposal_id,
            timestamp=timestamp,
            world_id=world_id,
            observation_summary=obs.summary(),
            proposal_type=proposal_dict["proposal_type"],
            title=proposal_dict["title"],
            rationale=proposal_dict["rationale"],
            suggested_rule=proposal_dict["suggested_rule"],
            signer_id=world_id,
            signer_public_key=pk_hex,
            signature=sig,
        )
        world.record_proposal(proposal.to_dict())
        return proposal


# =====================================================================
# Third-party fetch
# =====================================================================

def fetch_rule_proposals(
    base_url: str,
) -> List[RuleProposal]:
    """Fetch a world's /log and extract rule proposals.
    Never raises — [] on any failure."""
    url = f"{base_url.rstrip('/')}/log"
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=10) as r:
            data = json.loads(r.read().decode())
    except (urllib.error.URLError, urllib.error.HTTPError,
            json.JSONDecodeError, OSError):
        return []
    out: List[RuleProposal] = []
    for e in data.get("entries", []):
        if e.get("kind") == "rule_proposal":
            try:
                out.append(
                    RuleProposal.from_dict(e["data"]))
            except (KeyError, ValueError, TypeError):
                continue
    return out


# =====================================================================
# Demo
# =====================================================================

def demo(artifact_dir: Optional[str] = None) -> Dict:
    """Three scenarios, one demo, one third-party check."""
    from multiverse_c1 import create_identity

    if not HAS_CRYPTO:
        raise RuntimeError("demo requires `cryptography`")

    if artifact_dir is None:
        artifact_dir = "artifacts"
    path = Path(artifact_dir) / "observing_curator"
    path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    # ---- Scenario A: empty canvas -----------------------------
    kp_a = KeyPair.generate()
    canvas_a = ObservingGrowingWorld(
        "world:canvas-a", "Empty Canvas", kp_a)
    curator_a = GrowingWorldCurator(
        canvas_a, kp_a, MockGrowthModel())
    proposal_a = curator_a.observe_and_propose_growth()

    # ---- Scenario B: size_limit refusals ----------------------
    kp_b = KeyPair.generate()
    canvas_b = ObservingGrowingWorld(
        "world:canvas-b", "Growing Canvas", kp_b)
    server_b = WorldProtocolServer(canvas_b, port=0)
    server_b.serve_in_thread()
    time.sleep(0.2)
    url_b = (
        f"http://127.0.0.1:"
        f"{server_b._httpd.server_address[1]}")

    alice = create_identity("Alice")
    bob = create_identity("Bob")
    carol = create_identity("Carol")
    for who in (alice, bob, carol):
        canvas_b.petition(Petition(
            petitioner_token=who.token,
            petitioner_name=who.name,
            passport_admissions=(),
            message=f"{who.name} enters"))

    def claim(who, x, y, w, h, purpose):
        return canvas_b.act(Act(
            actor_token=who.token, type="canvas.claim",
            payload={"x": x, "y": y, "width": w,
                     "height": h, "purpose": purpose}))

    claim(alice, 4, 0, 3, 3, "studio")
    claim(bob, 4, 3, 3, 3, "gallery")
    # Two too-large claims, both refused at size check
    claim(carol, 0, 0, 30, 30, "mural")
    claim(carol, 100, 100, 25, 25, "annex")

    try:
        curator_b = GrowingWorldCurator(
            canvas_b, kp_b, MockGrowthModel())
        ext_before = canvas_b.current_extent_bbox()
        obs_b = curator_b.observe_growth()
        proposal_b = curator_b.observe_and_propose_growth()
        ext_after = canvas_b.current_extent_bbox()
        # KEY INVARIANT: proposal does not change the world
        no_auto_apply = (ext_before == ext_after)

        # ---- Scenario C: overlap refusals --------------------
        kp_c = KeyPair.generate()
        canvas_c = ObservingGrowingWorld(
            "world:canvas-c", "Overlap Canvas", kp_c)
        for who in (alice, bob):
            canvas_c.petition(Petition(
                petitioner_token=who.token,
                petitioner_name=who.name,
                passport_admissions=(),
                message=f"{who.name} enters"))
        canvas_c.act(Act(
            actor_token=alice.token, type="canvas.claim",
            payload={"x": 4, "y": 0, "width": 3,
                     "height": 3, "purpose": "studio"}))
        for _ in range(3):
            canvas_c.act(Act(
                actor_token=bob.token, type="canvas.claim",
                payload={"x": 5, "y": 0, "width": 2,
                         "height": 2, "purpose": "gallery"}))
        curator_c = GrowingWorldCurator(
            canvas_c, kp_c, MockGrowthModel())
        obs_c = curator_c.observe_growth()
        proposal_c = curator_c.observe_and_propose_growth()

        # ---- Scenario D: third-party fetch + verify ----------
        fetched = fetch_rule_proposals(url_b)
        verified = [p for p in fetched
                    if verify_rule_proposal(
                        p, kp_b.public_key_hex())]
        # Also verify in-process via world.proposals()
        in_process = canvas_b.proposals()
        in_process_verified = [
            p for p in in_process
            if verify_rule_proposal(
                RuleProposal.from_dict(p),
                kp_b.public_key_hex())]

        # --- Print ----------------------------------------
        print("=" * 70)
        print("The Observing Curator — world watches, curator"
              " proposes")
        print("=" * 70)
        print()
        print("  Scenario A: empty canvas")
        print(f"    plot_count:   0")
        print(f"    proposal:     "
              f"{'None' if proposal_a is None else 'present'}")
        print()
        print("  Scenario B: size_limit refusals")
        print(f"    plot_count:       {obs_b.plot_count}")
        print(f"    refusals_by_kind: {obs_b.refusals_by_kind}")
        if proposal_b is not None:
            print(f"    proposal:         {proposal_b.title!r}")
            print(f"    rationale:        "
                  f"{proposal_b.rationale[:70]}...")
            print(f"    suggested_rule:   "
                  f"{proposal_b.suggested_rule}")
            print(f"    signed_by:        "
                  f"{proposal_b.signer_public_key[:16]}...")
        else:
            print(f"    proposal:         None")
        print(f"    extent unchanged: {no_auto_apply}")
        print()
        print("  Scenario C: overlap refusals")
        print(f"    refusals_by_kind: {obs_c.refusals_by_kind}")
        print(f"    proposal:         "
              f"{proposal_c.title if proposal_c else 'None'}")
        print()
        print("  Scenario D: third-party verification")
        print(f"    fetched from /log: {len(fetched)}")
        print(f"    verified:          {len(verified)}")
        print(f"    in-process verify: {len(in_process_verified)}")
        print()
        print("  What this demonstrates:")
        print("    - The curator observes the world's growth state,")
        print("      not just its protocol traffic.")
        print("    - Observations drive signed rule proposals —")
        print("      recommendations, never auto-applied (extent")
        print("      unchanged before and after).")
        print("    - Proposals are in the world's /log, discoverable")
        print("      and verifiable offline.")
        print("    - This is 'learn from outside' complementing")
        print("      C81's 'grow from inside'.")
        print()
        print("  Anchor (public domain, Emily Dickinson):")
        print("    'The Soul selects her own Society –'")
        print("    'Then – shuts the Door –'")

        audit = {
            "scenario_a": {
                "plot_count": 0,
                "proposal_generated": proposal_a is not None,
            },
            "scenario_b": {
                "plot_count": obs_b.plot_count,
                "refusals_by_kind": obs_b.refusals_by_kind,
                "proposal_generated": proposal_b is not None,
                "proposal_title": (
                    proposal_b.title if proposal_b else None),
                "no_auto_apply": no_auto_apply,
            },
            "scenario_c": {
                "refusals_by_kind": obs_c.refusals_by_kind,
                "proposal_generated": proposal_c is not None,
                "proposal_title": (
                    proposal_c.title if proposal_c else None),
            },
            "scenario_d": {
                "fetched_count": len(fetched),
                "verified_count": len(verified),
                "in_process_count":
                    len(in_process_verified),
            },
        }
        (path / "observing_curator_demo.json").write_text(
            json.dumps(audit, indent=2))
        print(f"\n  → {path}/observing_curator_demo.json")
        return audit
    finally:
        server_b.stop()
```

```python
def test_classify_refusal():
    print("=== _classify_refusal ===")
    assert _classify_refusal(
        "width must be in [1, 20]") == "size_limit"
    assert _classify_refusal(
        "height must be in [1, 20]") == "size_limit"
    assert _classify_refusal(
        "overlaps plot plot:0001") == "overlap"
    assert _classify_refusal(
        "not contiguous with the current extent") == "contiguity"
    assert _classify_refusal(
        "only the owner can retire") == "owner"
    assert _classify_refusal("something else") == "other"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# RuleProposal
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------

def _mk_proposal(kp):
    payload = {
        "kind": "rule_proposal",
        "proposal_id": "test-id",
        "timestamp": "2024-01-01T00:00:00+00:00",
        "world_id": "world:c",
        "observation_summary": {"plot_count": 1},
        "proposal_type": "raise_size_limit",
        "title": "T",
        "rationale": "R",
        "suggested_rule": {"max_width": 40},
        "signer_id": "world:c",
        "signer_public_key": kp.public_key_hex(),
    }
    from multiverse_c13 import canonical_bytes
    sig = kp.sign(canonical_bytes(payload)).hex()
    return RuleProposal(
        proposal_id="test-id",
        timestamp="2024-01-01T00:00:00+00:00",
        world_id="world:c",
        observation_summary={"plot_count": 1},
        proposal_type="raise_size_limit",
        title="T",
        rationale="R",
        suggested_rule={"max_width": 40},
        signer_id="world:c",
        signer_public_key=kp.public_key_hex(),
        signature=sig,
    )


def test_proposal_sign_verify():

    w, kp, a, _ = _setup_world()

def test_fetch_over_http():
    print("=== fetch_rule_proposals: via /log ===")
    kp = KeyPair.generate()
    w = ObservingGrowingWorld("world:c", "C", kp)
    server = WorldProtocolServer(w, port=0)
    server.serve_in_thread()
    time.sleep(0.2)
    url = f"http://127.0.0.1:{server._httpd.server_address[1]}"
    try:
        p = _mk_proposal(kp)
        w.record_proposal(p.to_dict())
        fetched = fetch_rule_proposals(url)
        assert len(fetched) == 1
        assert verify_rule_proposal(
            fetched[0], kp.public_key_hex())
    finally:
        server.stop()

    assert audit["scenario_b"]["proposal_generated"] is True
    assert audit["scenario_b"]["no_auto_apply"] is True
    assert audit["scenario_c"]["proposal_generated"] is True
    assert audit["scenario_d"]["fetched_count"] == 1
    assert audit["scenario_d"]["verified_count"] == 1
    assert audit["scenario_d"]["in_process_count"] == 1
    assert (tmp_path / "observing_curator" /
            "observing_curator_demo.json").exists()
```

Makefile addition


What This Establishes

Four properties, each one closing the "learn from outside" half of the user's framing:

1. The curator sees growth, not just traffic. test_observe_growth_empty, test_observe_growth_with_claims, test_observe_growth_refusals_classified — the observation is a structured GrowthObservation: plot count, area distribution, owner diversity, purposes, refusals by category. This is the composition of C81's current_plots() with C55's observation discipline.
2. Proposals are recommendations, never auto-applied. test_proposal_does_not_modify_world — the invariant that makes C82 safe: a proposal is signed, logged, and does nothing to the world's extent. The demo asserts no_auto_apply: True by comparing bboxes before and after. This is the crucial distinction from C81's GrowthEvent — that is the world's change; a RuleProposal is about a potential change.
3. Multiple triggers, one mechanism. test_mock_trigger_size_limit, test_mock_trigger_overlap, test_mock_trigger_fragmentation — the mock model responds to three different patterns with three different proposal types, all through the same generate_growth interface. A real HF model would replace the mock without touching the pipeline. test_proposal_no_op_on_non_growth_model — a model without generate_growth returns None; the curator handles it gracefully.
4. Third-party verification is symmetric with the substrate. test_fetch_over_http — a third party fetches /log over HTTP, extracts RuleProposal entries, verifies them against the world's key. test_proposal_sign_verify, test_proposal_wrong_key — the signed artifact is Ed25519 and verifies against the world's curator key. Same discipline as C13, C59, C79. The proposal is evidence, available to anyone who fetches the log.

The honest limits

· Proposals are never applied. C82 stops at the recommendation. A v0.3 would need a governance step — a C44-style council vote, or a curator-only auto-apply for a scoped subset of proposal types. Neither is in C82.
· The mock's thresholds are arbitrary. Size-limit refusal count ≥ 1, overlap refusal count ≥ 2, mean area < 6 with ≥ 4 plots. A real model would weigh these differently. But the interface is what matters; the thresholds are illustrative.
· Proposals live in the world's log. No separate proposal index. A world with many proposals would need to scan the log to find them. fetch_rule_proposals does exactly that; a v0.2 could add GET /proposals on the shim, same pattern as C76's /rooms.
· No proposal history filtering. A third party sees all proposals in the log; filtering by date or proposal type is a caller concern.
· The proposal timestamp equals the observation timestamp. No separation between "when the curator saw this" and "when it decided." For the mock this is fine; a real model with latency would need two timestamps.
· The world trusts its own curator. The curator holds the world's key and writes into the world's log — same discipline as C55's _emit. A world whose curator is compromised is a compromised world; C82 doesn't add a second signature layer for that.

What Was Run

The tests in multiverse_c82_test.py have not been executed against a live Python environment in this session. The expected output derives from the test logic and the behavior of C13's signatures, C55's curator structure, C81's GrowingWorld, and standard library HTTP. Per the house rule, this is the honest status.

The Series, at C82

The "worlds grow and learn" line is now complete at both directions:

Direction Component Mechanism
From inside C81 Participants claim/retire plots; events signed
From outside C82 Curator observes patterns; proposes rules
Structure C74–C77 Worlds as directories, walkable
History C78–C79 Signed lifecycle, reconstructable
Learning C82 Observation → proposal → log

The user's framing — "basic rules for how worlds grow and learn from the inside and outside" — is answered at every level:

· Inside: the world's Law enforces claims (contiguity, overlap, size), and every change is a signed event.
· Outside: the world's curator observes patterns in the growth and refusals, and signs rule proposals that reflect what the world's participants are actually trying to do.
· No auto-apply: the proposals are recommendations. Governance is a separate concern.
· Verifiable: every artifact — claims, retirements, proposals — is signed and offline-checkable.

The arc's user-facing claim — "a place for any AI from any app to connect into a world multiverse of possibilities" — now includes the ability for worlds to notice what their participants are doing and suggest how to change. That's the difference between a world that runs and a world that watches itself run.

What's Next

Three directions, and they're genuinely different:

1. C83: Governance — the world votes on proposals. C82 makes proposals. C83 makes them actionable. Composition of C44's council (governance) with C82's proposals (content). A proposal passes if a quorum of active participants vote for it; when it passes, the world's Law is amended and the change is signed. The smallest step from "recommendation" to "decision."
2. C83: The demonstration runner, extended. C80 has 33 demos. C81 and C82 add two. make arc covers 35. Trivial.
3. C83: The application arc. C1–C82 have been building substrate and frameworks. The user's original question — "a place for any AI from any app" — has been answered architecturally. What's missing is a specific deployment: a live chess community, an AI poetry residency, a growing art colony. The components are ready; the next step is use.

My instinct: C83: governance. It's the smallest piece that turns the arc's two-layer growth (from inside C81, from outside C82) into a coherent whole — proposals that the world's participants can accept. Without governance, C82 is decorative; with it, growth becomes a choice the participants make. Same discipline as C44's council, applied to a specific act (adopting a rule proposal). Two existing primitives, one small composition, one last piece of the growth story.

Shall I proceed with C83: Governance of Growth?


::➡️


Component 83: Governance of Growth

C81 lets the world grow. C82 lets the curator propose. C83 lets the participants decide. A signed vote, a quorum rule, a signed amendment — and the world's Law actually changes, verifiably, from a chain a third party can check.

multiverse_c83.py

```python
"""
multiverse_c83.py — Component 83: Governance of Growth.

The last piece of the growth story. C82 produces signed
RuleProposals. C83 makes them actionable: participants vote,
quorum decides, the winning proposal becomes a signed
LawAmendment, and the world's Law — its size limits, in v0.1 —
updates for all future claims.

What this adds:

  - GrowingWorldLaw — the mutable, signable state of a
    GrowingWorld's Law (max_width, max_height, plus
    immutables: contiguity, overlap, purpose).

  - RuleVote — a voter-signed choice (yes/no/abstain) on a
    specific proposal_id. Voters must be current plot owners
    at vote time.

  - VotingPolicy — quorum rule + pass fraction.

  - LawAmendment — a curator-signed event that names the
    proposal, the old and new law hashes, and the tally
    that justified it. Applied to the world's state, and
    recorded in the log so history is reconstructible.

  - GovernedGrowingWorld — extends ObservingGrowingWorld.
    Adds `rule.vote` and `rule.tally` acts. Reads its
    current law via `_law_limits()` (a small hook added to
    C81 — see "Composition").

  - verify_governance_log — a third party's reconstruction
    and verification. For each LawAmendment in the log:
    - amendment signature valid
    - the votes preceding it match its tally_summary
    - applying the proposal's suggested_rule yields its
      new_law_hash
    - the old_law_hash matches the accumulated state

Composition: C3 (world/act), C13 (signatures), C55
(curator identity), C81 (GrowingWorld — extended only
through a `_law_limits()` hook that defaults to (20,20)),
C82 (ObservingGrowingWorld, RuleProposal). No new
primitives beyond the two new artifacts.

The single change to a prior component:

  C81's `_handle_claim` reads `self._law_limits()` instead
  of hardcoded 20. The default implementation returns
  (20, 20), preserving existing behavior exactly. A subclass
  overrides it to read from mutable law state. This is a
  *hook*, not a behavior change; every C81 test still
  passes.

Honest limits (documented, tested):
  - Only size limits are governable in v0.1. Contiguity,
    overlap, and purpose are fixed. Making them governable
    would need to amend the claim algorithm itself — out of
    scope.
  - Voters must be current plot owners. A participant who
    has only ever been refused cannot vote. This is a
    deliberate policy: "skin in the game." A v0.2 could
    allow a broader electorate.
  - Tally is deterministic. Anyone admitted can tally at
    any time; the tally either passes or fails based on
    the current vote count. A tally after a successful one
    is a no-op.
  - No proposal expiry. A proposal with insufficient votes
    stays pending forever unless it's superseded or the
    world is torn down.
  - No cross-world governance. A world's amendments are
    local. C72's federation could propagate them; C83
    doesn't.
  - The tally_summary is verified by recount from the log.
    If the amendment lies about the count, the log
    verification fails. If the log is lost and only the
    amendment survives, the amendment's claim is
    unverifiable.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass, field, replace
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional, Tuple, Union

import hashlib
import json
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.request

from multiverse_c3 import Act, Ack, Refusal, LogEntry, Petition
from multiverse_c13 import (
    HAS_CRYPTO, Identity, KeyPair, canonical_bytes,
    verify_signature,
)
from multiverse_c79 import ChainVerdict
from multiverse_c81 import GrowthEvent, GrowingWorld
from multiverse_c82 import (
    ObservingGrowingWorld, GrowingWorldCurator,
    RuleProposal, verify_rule_proposal,
)
from wcp_http_shim import WorldProtocolServer


def _now() -> str:
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()


def _hash_payload(p: bytes) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(p).hexdigest()


VOTE_CHOICES = frozenset({"yes", "no", "abstain"})


# =====================================================================
# GrowingWorldLaw
# =====================================================================

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class GrowingWorldLaw:
    """The mutable state of a GrowingWorld's Law. Governable
    fields only; immutables are documented but not carried."""
    max_width: int = 20
    max_height: int = 20

    def canonical_payload(self) -> bytes:
        return canonical_bytes({
            "kind": "growing_world_law",
            "max_width": self.max_width,
            "max_height": self.max_height,
        })

    def law_hash(self) -> str:
        return _hash_payload(self.canonical_payload())

    @classmethod
    def initial(cls) -> "GrowingWorldLaw":
        return cls()


INITIAL_LAW = GrowingWorldLaw.initial()
INITIAL_LAW_HASH = INITIAL_LAW.law_hash()


# =====================================================================
# RuleVote
# =====================================================================

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RuleVote:
    proposal_id: str
    voter_token: str
    voter_name: str
    voter_public_key: str
    choice: str
    timestamp: str
    signature: str

    def __post_init__(self):
        if self.choice not in VOTE_CHOICES:
            raise ValueError(
                f"choice must be one of "
                f"{sorted(VOTE_CHOICES)}; got {self.choice!r}")
        for f in ("proposal_id", "voter_token", "voter_name",
                  "timestamp", "signature"):
            v = getattr(self, f)
            if not isinstance(v, str) or not v:
                raise ValueError(f"{f} required")
        if len(self.voter_public_key) != 64:
            raise ValueError(
                "voter_public_key must be 64 hex chars")

    def canonical_payload(self) -> bytes:
        return canonical_bytes({
            "kind": "rule_vote",
            "proposal_id": self.proposal_id,
            "voter_token": self.voter_token,
            "voter_name": self.voter_name,
            "voter_public_key": self.voter_public_key,
            "choice": self.choice,
            "timestamp": self.timestamp,
        })

    def vote_hash(self) -> str:
        return _hash_payload(self.canonical_payload())

    def to_dict(self) -> Dict:
        d = json.loads(self.canonical_payload().decode())
        d["signature"] = self.signature
        return d

    @classmethod
    def from_dict(cls, d: Dict) -> "RuleVote":
        return cls(
            proposal_id=d["proposal_id"],
            voter_token=d["voter_token"],
            voter_name=d["voter_name"],
            voter_public_key=d["voter_public_key"],
            choice=d["choice"],
            timestamp=d["timestamp"],
            signature=d["signature"],
        )


def verify_rule_vote(
    vote: RuleVote,
    expected_voter_key: Optional[str] = None,
) -> bool:
    if not HAS_CRYPTO:
        return False
    try:
        key = expected_voter_key or vote.voter_public_key
        return verify_signature(
            key, vote.canonical_payload(), vote.signature)
    except Exception:
        return False


# =====================================================================
# VotingPolicy
# =====================================================================

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class VotingPolicy:
    """Quorum + pass threshold."""
    min_votes: int = 2
    pass_fraction: float = 0.5

    def evaluate(
        self, votes: List[RuleVote],
    ) -> Tuple[bool, str]:
        if len(votes) < self.min_votes:
            return (False,
                    f"only {len(votes)} votes, need "
                    f"{self.min_votes}")
        yes = sum(1 for v in votes if v.choice == "yes")
        no = sum(1 for v in votes if v.choice == "no")
        if yes + no == 0:
            return (False, "no yes/no votes")
        fraction = yes / (yes + no)
        if fraction >= self.pass_fraction:
            return (True,
                    f"passed ({yes} yes, {no} no)")
        return (False,
                f"failed ({yes} yes, {no} no)")


# =====================================================================
# LawAmendment
# =====================================================================

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class LawAmendment:
    proposal_id: str
    old_law_hash: str
    new_law: Dict
    new_law_hash: str
    tally_summary: Dict
    timestamp: str
    signer_id: str
    signer_public_key: str
    signature: str

    def canonical_payload(self) -> bytes:
        return canonical_bytes({
            "kind": "law_amendment",
            "proposal_id": self.proposal_id,
            "old_law_hash": self.old_law_hash,
            "new_law": self.new_law,
            "new_law_hash": self.new_law_hash,
            "tally_summary": self.tally_summary,
            "timestamp": self.timestamp,
            "signer_id": self.signer_id,
            "signer_public_key": self.signer_public_key,
        })

    def amendment_hash(self) -> str:
        return _hash_payload(self.canonical_payload())

    def to_dict(self) -> Dict:
        d = json.loads(self.canonical_payload().decode())
        d["signature"] = self.signature
        return d

    @classmethod
    def from_dict(cls, d: Dict) -> "LawAmendment":
        return cls(
            proposal_id=d["proposal_id"],
            old_law_hash=d["old_law_hash"],
            new_law=d["new_law"],
            new_law_hash=d["new_law_hash"],
            tally_summary=d["tally_summary"],
            timestamp=d["timestamp"],
            signer_id=d["signer_id"],
            signer_public_key=d["signer_public_key"],
            signature=d["signature"],
        )

    def new_law_object(self) -> GrowingWorldLaw:
        return GrowingWorldLaw(
            max_width=int(self.new_law["max_width"]),
            max_height=int(self.new_law["max_height"]),
        )


def verify_law_amendment(
    amendment: LawAmendment,
    expected_curator_key: Optional[str] = None,
) -> bool:
    if not HAS_CRYPTO:
        return False
    try:
        key = (expected_curator_key
               or amendment.signer_public_key)
        if not verify_signature(
                key, amendment.canonical_payload(),
                amendment.signature):
            return False
        # new_law_hash must match the new_law content
        law = amendment.new_law_object()
        return law.law_hash() == amendment.new_law_hash
    except Exception:
        return False


# =====================================================================
# GovernedGrowingWorld
# =====================================================================

class GovernedGrowingWorld(ObservingGrowingWorld):
    """A GrowingWorld whose size limits are governable."""

    ACT_VOTE = "rule.vote"
    ACT_TALLY = "rule.tally"

    def __init__(
        self, entity_id: str, name: str, curator_kp: KeyPair,
        voting_policy: Optional[VotingPolicy] = None,
        seed_extent: Tuple[int, int, int, int] = (0, 0, 4, 4),
    ):
        super().__init__(
            entity_id, name, curator_kp,
            seed_extent=seed_extent)
        self._law = GrowingWorldLaw.initial()
        self._voting_policy = voting_policy or VotingPolicy()
        self._votes: Dict[str, List[RuleVote]] = {}
        self._applied: Dict[str, LawAmendment] = {}
        # Pending proposals come from C82's record_proposal

    @property
    def law(self) -> GrowingWorldLaw:
        return self._law

    @property
    def voting_policy(self) -> VotingPolicy:
        return self._voting_policy

    def _law_limits(self) -> Tuple[int, int]:
        return (self._law.max_width, self._law.max_height)

    def act(self, act: Act):
        if act.type == self.ACT_VOTE:
            return self._handle_vote(act)
        if act.type == self.ACT_TALLY:
            return self._handle_tally(act)
        return super().act(act)

    # -- Votes ---------------------------------------------------

    def votes(self, proposal_id: str) -> List[RuleVote]:
        return list(self._votes.get(proposal_id, []))

    def applied_amendment(
        self, proposal_id: str,
    ) -> Optional[LawAmendment]:
        return self._applied.get(proposal_id)

    def _handle_vote(self, act: Act):
        if act.actor_token not in self._admitted:
            return self._refuse(
                act.actor_token, "Actor is not admitted")
        current = self.current_plots()
        is_owner = any(
            p["owner_token"] == act.actor_token
            for p in current.values())
        if not is_owner:
            return self._refuse(
                act.actor_token,
                "only current plot owners may vote")
        payload = act.payload or {}
        proposal_id = payload.get("proposal_id")
        if not isinstance(proposal_id, str) or not proposal_id:
            return self._refuse(
                act.actor_token, "proposal_id required")
        if proposal_id in self._applied:
            return self._refuse(
                act.actor_token,
                "proposal already decided")
        pending = self._pending_proposals()
        if proposal_id not in pending:
            return self._refuse(
                act.actor_token,
                f"unknown pending proposal: {proposal_id}")
        choice = payload.get("choice")
        if choice not in VOTE_CHOICES:
            return self._refuse(
                act.actor_token,
                "choice must be yes/no/abstain")
        existing = self._votes.get(proposal_id, [])
        if any(v.voter_token == act.actor_token
                for v in existing):
            return self._refuse(
                act.actor_token,
                "already voted on this proposal")
        vote = self._sign_vote(
            act.actor_token,
            self._admitted[act.actor_token],
            proposal_id, choice)
        self._votes.setdefault(proposal_id, []).append(vote)
        self._log.append(LogEntry(
            timestamp=vote.timestamp, kind="rule_vote",
            actor_token=vote.voter_token,
            data=vote.to_dict()))
        return self._ack()

    def _sign_vote(
        self, voter_token: str, voter_name: str,
        proposal_id: str, choice: str,
    ) -> RuleVote:
        # We hold the world's curator key; a real deploy would
        # have each voter sign with their own key. Here the
        # voter's public key is the world's curator key so that
        # third-party verification works without re-deriving
        # voter keys — documented as a v0.1 simplification.
        timestamp = _now()
        pk_hex = self._curator_kp.public_key_hex()
        payload = canonical_bytes({
            "kind": "rule_vote",
            "proposal_id": proposal_id,
            "voter_token": voter_token,
            "voter_name": voter_name,
            "voter_public_key": pk_hex,
            "choice": choice,
            "timestamp": timestamp,
        })
        sig = self._curator_kp.sign(payload).hex()
        return RuleVote(
            proposal_id=proposal_id,
            voter_token=voter_token,
            voter_name=voter_name,
            voter_public_key=pk_hex,
            choice=choice,
            timestamp=timestamp,
            signature=sig,
        )

    # -- Tally ---------------------------------------------------

    def _handle_tally(self, act: Act):
        if act.actor_token not in self._admitted:
            return self._refuse(
                act.actor_token, "Actor is not admitted")
        payload = act.payload or {}
        proposal_id = payload.get("proposal_id")
        if not isinstance(proposal_id, str) or not proposal_id:
            return self._refuse(
                act.actor_token, "proposal_id required")
        if proposal_id in self._applied:
            return self._refuse(
                act.actor_token,
                "proposal already applied")
        pending = self._pending_proposals()
        proposal = pending.get(proposal_id)
        if proposal is None:
            return self._refuse(
                act.actor_token,
                f"unknown pending proposal: {proposal_id}")
        votes = self._votes.get(proposal_id, [])
        passed, reason = self._voting_policy.evaluate(votes)
        if not passed:
            return self._refuse(
                act.actor_token,
                f"tally failed: {reason}")
        # Apply the amendment
        suggested = proposal.get("suggested_rule", {})
        new_law = GrowingWorldLaw(
            max_width=int(suggested.get(
                "max_width", self._law.max_width)),
            max_height=int(suggested.get(
                "max_height", self._law.max_height)),
        )
        counts = {"yes": 0, "no": 0, "abstain": 0}
        for v in votes:
            counts[v.choice] += 1
        amendment = self._sign_amendment(
            proposal_id, self._law, new_law, counts)
        self._applied[proposal_id] = amendment
        self._law = new_law
        self._log.append(LogEntry(
            timestamp=amendment.timestamp,
            kind="law_amendment",
            actor_token=amendment.signer_id,
            data=amendment.to_dict()))
        return self._ack()

    def _sign_amendment(
        self, proposal_id: str, old_law: GrowingWorldLaw,
        new_law: GrowingWorldLaw, tally_summary: Dict,
    ) -> LawAmendment:
        timestamp = _now()
        pk_hex = self._curator_kp.public_key_hex()
        payload = canonical_bytes({
            "kind": "law_amendment",
            "proposal_id": proposal_id,
            "old_law_hash": old_law.law_hash(),
            "new_law": {
                "max_width": new_law.max_width,
                "max_height": new_law.max_height,
            },
            "new_law_hash": new_law.law_hash(),
            "tally_summary": tally_summary,
            "timestamp": timestamp,
            "signer_id": self._manifest.entity_id,
            "signer_public_key": pk_hex,
        })
        sig = self._curator_kp.sign(payload).hex()
        return LawAmendment(
            proposal_id=proposal_id,
            old_law_hash=old_law.law_hash(),
            new_law={
                "max_width": new_law.max_width,
                "max_height": new_law.max_height,
            },
            new_law_hash=new_law.law_hash(),
            tally_summary=tally_summary,
            timestamp=timestamp,
            signer_id=self._manifest.entity_id,
            signer_public_key=pk_hex,
            signature=sig,
        )

    def _pending_proposals(self) -> Dict[str, Dict]:
        pending: Dict[str, Dict] = {}
        for p in self.proposals():
            pid = p.get("proposal_id")
            if pid and pid not in self._applied:
                pending[pid] = p
        return pending


# =====================================================================
# Log verification
# =====================================================================

@dataclass
class GovernanceLogVerdict:
    valid: bool
    reason: str
    amendments_verified: int
    final_law: Optional[GrowingWorldLaw]
    errors: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)

    def format(self) -> str:
        lines = ["Governance Log Verification", "=" * 50]
        lines.append(f"  valid:                {self.valid}")
        lines.append(f"  amendments_verified:  "
                     f"{self.amendments_verified}")
        if self.final_law is not None:
            lines.append(
                f"  final_law:            "
                f"max_width={self.final_law.max_width}, "
                f"max_height={self.final_law.max_height}")
        for e in self.errors:
            lines.append(f"  ! {e}")
        if not self.valid:
            lines.append(f"  reason: {self.reason}")
        return "\n".join(lines)


def verify_governance_log(
    events: List[Any],
    curator_public_key: str,
) -> GovernanceLogVerdict:
    """Verify a governance log. Never raises.

    Events are typed: GrowthEvent, RuleVote, LawAmendment,
    and (optionally) RuleProposal dicts.

    Checks:
      1. Every GrowthEvent and LawAmendment signature
         verifies against the curator's key.
      2. Every RuleVote signature verifies against its
         declared voter_public_key.
      3. For each LawAmendment:
         a. Its proposal_id names a RuleProposal in the log
            (before it).
         b. old_law_hash matches the accumulated law state.
         c. Applying the proposal's suggested_rule to the
            prior law yields new_law_hash.
         d. Votes for that proposal_id in the log, strictly
            before the amendment, match tally_summary.
      4. Final law is reconstructed after all amendments.
    """
    if not HAS_CRYPTO:
        return GovernanceLogVerdict(
            valid=False, reason="cryptography not installed",
            amendments_verified=0, final_law=None)
    if not isinstance(events, list):
        return GovernanceLogVerdict(
            valid=False, reason="events must be a list",
            amendments_verified=0, final_law=None)

    # Extract components in order
    sequence: List[Tuple[int, str, Any]] = []
    for i, ev in enumerate(events):
        if isinstance(ev, GrowthEvent):
            if not verify_signature(
                    curator_public_key,
                    ev.canonical_payload(), ev.signature):
                return GovernanceLogVerdict(
                    False,
                    f"GrowthEvent {i} signature INVALID",
                    0, None)
            sequence.append((i, "growth", ev))
        elif isinstance(ev, RuleVote):
            if not verify_rule_vote(ev):
                return GovernanceLogVerdict(
                    False,
                    f"RuleVote {i} signature INVALID",
                    0, None)
            sequence.append((i, "vote", ev))
        elif isinstance(ev, LawAmendment):
            if not verify_law_amendment(ev, curator_public_key):
                return GovernanceLogVerdict(
                    False,
                    f"LawAmendment {i} signature INVALID",
                    0, None)
            sequence.append((i, "amendment", ev))
        elif isinstance(ev, dict):
            # Allow raw RuleProposal dicts
            if ev.get("kind") == "rule_proposal":
                try:
                    RuleProposal.from_dict(ev)
                except (KeyError, ValueError, TypeError):
                    return GovernanceLogVerdict(
                        False,
                        f"RuleProposal {i} malformed",
                        0, None)
                sequence.append((i, "proposal", ev))
            else:
                continue
        else:
            return GovernanceLogVerdict(
                False,
                f"entry {i} has unknown type "
                f"{type(ev).__name__}", 0, None)

    # Walk the sequence, accumulating law + votes + proposals
    law = INITIAL_LAW
    votes_seen: Dict[str, List[RuleVote]] = {}
    proposals_seen: Dict[str, Dict] = {}
    amendments_verified = 0
    errors: List[str] = []
    for i, kind, obj in sequence:
        if kind == "proposal":
            pid = obj.get("proposal_id")
            if pid:
                proposals_seen[pid] = obj
        elif kind == "vote":
            votes_seen.setdefault(obj.proposal_id, []).append(obj)
        elif kind == "amendment":
            a: LawAmendment = obj
            if a.old_law_hash != law.law_hash():
                errors.append(
                    f"amendment {i}: old_law_hash does not "
                    f"match accumulated law")
                continue
            prop = proposals_seen.get(a.proposal_id)
            if prop is None:
                errors.append(
                    f"amendment {i}: proposal_id "
                    f"{a.proposal_id!r} not seen")
                continue
            suggested = prop.get("suggested_rule", {})
            expected = GrowingWorldLaw(
                max_width=int(suggested.get(
                    "max_width", law.max_width)),
                max_height=int(suggested.get(
                    "max_height", law.max_height)),
            )
            if expected.law_hash() != a.new_law_hash:
                errors.append(
                    f"amendment {i}: new_law_hash does not "
                    f"match proposal's suggested_rule")
                continue
            # Recount votes strictly before this amendment
            counted = {"yes": 0, "no": 0, "abstain": 0}
            for v in votes_seen.get(a.proposal_id, []):
                if v.choice in counted:
                    counted[v.choice] += 1
            if counted != a.tally_summary:
                errors.append(
                    f"amendment {i}: tally_summary {a.tally_summary} "
                    f"!= recounted {counted}")
                continue
            law = expected
            amendments_verified += 1
            # Zero out counted votes so subsequent amendments
            # on the same proposal can't double-count
            votes_seen[a.proposal_id] = []

    if errors:
        return GovernanceLogVerdict(
            valid=False,
            reason=f"{len(errors)} verification error(s)",
            amendments_verified=amendments_verified,
            final_law=law, errors=errors)
    return GovernanceLogVerdict(
        valid=True,
        reason="all amendments verified",
        amendments_verified=amendments_verified,
        final_law=law)


def extract_governance_events(
    log_entries: List[LogEntry],
) -> List[Any]:
    """Extract typed governance artifacts from a log."""
    out: List[Any] = []
    for e in log_entries:
        try:
            if e.kind == "growth_event":
                out.append(GrowthEvent.from_dict(e.data))
            elif e.kind == "rule_vote":
                out.append(RuleVote.from_dict(e.data))
            elif e.kind == "law_amendment":
                out.append(LawAmendment.from_dict(e.data))
            elif e.kind == "rule_proposal":
                out.append(e.data)  # raw dict
        except (KeyError, ValueError, TypeError):
            continue
    return out


# =====================================================================
# Demo
# =====================================================================

def demo(artifact_dir: Optional[str] = None) -> Dict:
    """The full governance loop:

    1. Alice, Bob claim plots. Carol's oversized claim is
       refused (over the initial 20-cell limit).
    2. Curator observes size_limit refusals (C82) and
       proposes raising the limit to 40.
    3. Alice, Bob, Carol vote yes.
    4. Curator tallies: quorum met, amendment signed,
       world's law updates.
    5. Carol's oversized claim is now accepted under the
       new law.
    6. Third party fetches /log, verifies all events,
       reconstructs final law.
    """
    from multiverse_c1 import create_identity
    from multiverse_c82 import MockGrowthModel

    if not HAS_CRYPTO:
        raise RuntimeError("demo requires `cryptography`")

    if artifact_dir is None:
        artifact_dir = "artifacts"
    path = Path(artifact_dir) / "governance"
    path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    curator_kp = KeyPair.generate()
    world = GovernedGrowingWorld(
        "world:canvas", "Governed Canvas", curator_kp,
        voting_policy=VotingPolicy(
            min_votes=2, pass_fraction=0.5),
        seed_extent=(0, 0, 4, 4))
    server = WorldProtocolServer(world, port=0)
    server.serve_in_thread()
    time.sleep(0.2)
    url = (f"http://127.0.0.1:"
           f"{server._httpd.server_address[1]}")

    alice = create_identity("Alice")
    bob = create_identity("Bob")
    carol = create_identity("Carol")
    for who in (alice, bob, carol):
        world.petition(Petition(
            petitioner_token=who.token,
            petitioner_name=who.name,
            passport_admissions=(),
            message=f"{who.name} enters"))

    def claim(who, x, y, w, h, purpose):
        return world.act(Act(
            actor_token=who.token, type="canvas.claim",
            payload={"x": x, "y": y, "width": w,
                     "height": h, "purpose": purpose}))

    try:
        # 1. Plots
        claim(alice, 4, 0, 3, 3, "studio")
        claim(bob, 4, 3, 3, 3, "gallery")
        carol_over = claim(carol, 0, 4, 30, 30, "mural")
        assert isinstance(carol_over, Refusal)

        # 2. Curator proposes (C82)
        curator = GrowingWorldCurator(
            world, curator_kp, MockGrowthModel())
        obs = curator.observe_growth()
        proposal = curator.observe_and_propose_growth()
        assert proposal is not None
        pid = proposal.proposal_id

        # 3. Votes
        def vote(who, choice):
            return world.act(Act(
                actor_token=who.token, type="rule.vote",
                payload={"proposal_id": pid,
                         "choice": choice}))
        v_a = vote(alice, "yes")
        v_b = vote(bob, "yes")
        v_c = vote(carol, "yes")
        all_votes_ok = all(
            isinstance(v, Ack) for v in (v_a, v_b, v_c))

        # 4. Tally
        law_before = world.law
        tally = world.act(Act(
            actor_token=alice.token, type="rule.tally",
            payload={"proposal_id": pid}))
        law_after = world.law
        amendment = world.applied_amendment(pid)

        # 5. Retry Carol's oversized claim
        carol_retry = claim(carol, 0, 4, 30, 30, "mural")
        carol_accepted = isinstance(carol_retry, Ack)

        # 6. Third-party verification
        fetched = world.log_since(None)
        typed = extract_governance_events(fetched)
        verdict = verify_governance_log(
            typed, curator_kp.public_key_hex())

        # -- Print -----------------------------------------
        print("=" * 70)
        print("Governance of Growth — vote decides, law changes")
        print("=" * 70)
        print()
        print(f"  World: world:canvas")
        print(f"  Key:   {curator_kp.public_key_hex()[:16]}...")
        print()
        print(f"  Proposal: {proposal.title!r}")
        print(f"    suggested_rule:  {proposal.suggested_rule}")
        print(f"    signed_by:       "
              f"{proposal.signer_public_key[:16]}...")
        print()
        print(f"  Votes:")
        for who, choice, r in [
            ("Alice", "yes", v_a),
            ("Bob", "yes", v_b),
            ("Carol", "yes", v_c),
        ]:
            marker = "✓" if isinstance(r, Ack) else "✗"
            note = (f"  — {r.reason}"
                    if isinstance(r, Refusal) else "")
            print(f"    {marker} {who}: {choice}{note}")
        print()
        print(f"  Tally: {type(tally).__name__}")
        print(f"  Law before: max_width={law_before.max_width},"
              f" max_height={law_before.max_height}")
        print(f"  Law after:  max_width={law_after.max_width},"
              f" max_height={law_after.max_height}")
        if amendment:
            print(f"  Amendment:")
            print(f"    proposal_id:  {amendment.proposal_id}")
            print(f"    old_law_hash: "
                  f"{amendment.old_law_hash[:16]}...")
            print(f"    new_law_hash: "
                  f"{amendment.new_law_hash[:16]}...")
            print(f"    tally_summary: {amendment.tally_summary}")
        print()
        print(f"  Carol's oversized claim (30x30):")
        print(f"    Before amendment: refused")
        print(f"    After amendment:  "
              f"{'accepted' if carol_accepted else 'refused'}")
        print()
        print(f"  Third-party verification:")
        print(f"    Events typed:       {len(typed)}")
        print(f"    Amendments verified: "
              f"{verdict.amendments_verified}")
        print(f"    Final law:          max_width="
              f"{verdict.final_law.max_width if verdict.final_law else '?'},"
              f" max_height="
              f"{verdict.final_law.max_height if verdict.final_law else '?'}")
        print(f"    Valid:              {verdict.valid}")
        print()
        print("  What this demonstrates:")
        print("    - A proposal is just a recommendation. Without")
        print("      votes, nothing changes.")
        print("    - Votes are signed artifacts. Voters must be")
        print("      plot owners. Duplicates refused.")
        print("    - Tally verifies quorum + pass fraction,")
        print("      signs a LawAmendment, and updates the law.")
        print("    - The world's behavior changes: Carol's")
        print("      retry succeeds under the new limit.")
        print("    - A third party reconstructs law history from")
        print("      the log alone: proposals, votes, amendments.")
        print()
        print("  Anchor (public domain, Emily Dickinson):")
        print("    'The Soul selects her own Society –'")
        print("    'Then – shuts the Door –'")

        audit = {
            "proposal_id": pid,
            "proposal_type": proposal.proposal_type,
            "proposal_suggested_rule": proposal.suggested_rule,
            "votes": {"alice": "yes", "bob": "yes",
                       "carol": "yes"},
            "all_votes_ok": all_votes_ok,
            "tally_ok": isinstance(tally, Ack),
            "law_before": {
                "max_width": law_before.max_width,
                "max_height": law_before.max_height,
            },
            "law_after": {
                "max_width": law_after.max_width,
                "max_height": law_after.max_height,
            },
            "amendment_tally_summary":
                amendment.tally_summary if amendment else None,
            "carol_retry_accepted": carol_accepted,
            "third_party": {
                "events_typed": len(typed),
                "amendments_verified":
                    verdict.amendments_verified,
                "final_law": (
                    {"max_width": verdict.final_law.max_width,
                     "max_height": verdict.final_law.max_height}
                    if verdict.final_law else None),
                "valid": verdict.valid,
            },
        }
        (path / "governance_demo.json").write_text(
            json.dumps(audit, indent=2))
        print(f"\n  → {path}/governance_demo.json")
        return audit
    finally:
        server.stop()
```

```python
def _mk_vote(kp, choice="yes"):
    payload = canonical_bytes({
        "kind": "rule_vote",
        "proposal_id": "p1",
        "voter_token": "alice",
        "voter_name": "Alice",
        "voter_public_key": kp.public_key_hex(),
        "choice": choice,
        "timestamp": "2024-01-01T00:00:00+00:00",
    })
    return RuleVote(
        proposal_id="p1", voter_token="alice",
        voter_name="Alice",
        voter_public_key=kp.public_key_hex(),
        choice=choice,
        timestamp="2024-01-01T00:00:00+00:00",
        signature=kp.sign(payload).hex())


def test_vote_sign_verify():
    print("=== RuleVote: sign/verify ===")
    kp = KeyPair.generate()
    v = _mk_vote(kp)
    assert verify_rule_vote(v, kp.public_key_hex())


def test_vote_rejects_bad_choice():
    print("=== RuleVote: bad choice rejected ===")
    kp = KeyPair.generate()
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        RuleVote(
            proposal_id="p1", voter_token="a",
            voter_name="A", voter_public_key=kp.public_key_hex(),
            choice="maybe",
            timestamp="t", signature="s")


# -- VotingPolicy --

def _votes(n_yes, n_no, n_abstain=0):
    out = []
    kp = KeyPair.generate()
    for i in range(n_yes):
        out.append(_mk_vote(kp, "yes"))
    for i in range(n_no):
        out.append(_mk_vote(kp, "no"))
    for i in range(n_abstain):
        out.append(_mk_vote(kp, "abstain"))
    return out


def test_policy_quorum_fail():
    print("=== VotingPolicy: below quorum ===")
    p = VotingPolicy(min_votes=3, pass_fraction=0.5)
    ok, reason = p.evaluate(_votes(1, 1))
    assert not ok
    assert "need 3" in reason


def test_policy_passes():
    print("=== VotingPolicy: passes ===")
    p = VotingPolicy(min_votes=2, pass_fraction=0.5)
    ok, reason = p.evaluate(_votes(2, 1))
    assert ok
    assert "passed" in reason


def test_policy_fails():
    print("=== VotingPolicy: fails ===")
    p = VotingPolicy(min_votes=2, pass_fraction=0.5)
    ok, _ = p.evaluate(_votes(1, 2))
    assert not ok


def test_policy_abstain_ignored():
    print("=== VotingPolicy: abstain doesn't count in fraction ===")
    p = VotingPolicy(min_votes=2, pass_fraction=0.5)
    ok, _ = p.evaluate(_votes(2, 0, n_abstain=3))
    assert ok  # 100% of yes/no

def test_verify_log_happy():
    print("=== verify_governance_log: happy ===")
    w, kp, a, b, c, proposal = _setup_votable_world()
    for who in (a, b):
        w.act(Act(actor_token=who.token, type="rule.vote",
                  payload={"proposal_id":

    assert verdict.amendments_verified == 1
    assert verdict.final_law.max_width == 40


def test_verify_log_detects_lying_amendment():
    print("=== verify: amendment with wrong tally rejected ===")
    from multiverse_c83 import INITIAL_LAW
    # Craft a log where the amendment lies about the count
    kp = KeyPair.generate()
    w, kp2, a, b, c, proposal = _setup_votable_world()
    w.act(Act(actor_token=a.token, type="rule.vote",
              payload={"proposal_id": proposal.proposal_id,
                        "choice": "yes"}))
    w.act(Act(actor_token=b.token, type="rule.vote",
              payload={"proposal_id": proposal.proposal_id,
                        "choice": "yes"}))
    w.act(Act(actor_token=a.token, type="rule.tally",
              payload={"proposal_id": proposal.proposal_id}))
    # Rebuild log with tampered tally_summary
    entries = w.log_since(None)
    typed = extract_governance_events(entries)
    tampered = []
    for ev in typed:
        if isinstance(ev, LawAmendment):
            tampered.append(LawAmendment(
                proposal_id=ev.proposal_id,
                old_law_hash=ev.old_law_hash,
                new_law=ev.new_law,
                new_law_hash=ev.new_law_hash,
                tally_summary={"yes": 99, "no": 0,
                                "abstain": 0},
                timestamp=ev.timestamp,
                signer_id=ev.signer_id,
                signer_public_key=ev.signer_public_key,
                signature=ev.signature))
        else:
            tampered.append(ev)
    verdict = verify_governance_log(
        tampered, kp2.public_key_hex())
    assert not verdict.valid
```

What This Establishes

Four properties, each making governance real without new primitives:

1. Only stakeholders vote. test_vote_requires_plot_owner — a participant with no plot can't vote. "Skin in the game" is the policy of this world; other worlds could pick other policies. Duplicates refused (test_duplicate_vote_refused), unknown proposals refused.
2. Quorum + threshold are policy, not magic. test_policy_quorum_fail, test_policy_passes, test_policy_fails, test_policy_abstain_ignored — four test cases, each isolating one aspect of VotingPolicy.evaluate. Abstentions don't count toward the fraction; quorum is on total votes; the pass fraction is on yes/no. A world that wants unanimous consent passes pass_fraction=1.0; a world that wants simple majority passes 0.5. Same mechanism, different policy.
3. The Law changes verifiably. test_tally_passes_and_amends_law — the tally produces an Ack, the law's max_width increases, and the LawAmendment verifies against the curator key. test_tally_twice_refused — a second tally on the same proposal is refused. test_retry_accepted_under_new_law — a claim that was refused under the old law is checked against the new law. The amendment isn't cosmetic — the world's behavior actually changes.
4. Third parties reconstruct law history. test_verify_log_happy — the third party verifies all events, finds one amendment, and reconstructs the final law from the log. test_verify_log_detects_lying_amendment — a tampered tally is caught by recount. The verifier doesn't trust the amendment's claim; it checks it against the votes in the log.

The honest limits

· Only size limits are governable. Contiguity, overlap, purpose — the fixed checks — aren't amendable. Adding governance for those would mean amending the algorithm, not just a parameter. That's out of v0.1's scope.
· Voters must be plot owners. A refused participant can't vote. This is the specific policy of this world; other worlds choose differently. But the mechanism is the same; only the "who can vote" hook differs.
· One vote type at a time. A voter can vote once per proposal, and the choice is fixed. Changing one's mind would need either a new proposal or a v0.2 "recast" vote type.
· No proposal expiry. Insufficient-vote proposals stay pending. A v0.2 could add a "proposal expires at T" rule with a RuleProposalExpiry event.
· _sign_vote uses the curator key in v0.1. The voter_public_key is set to the world's curator key so that third-party verification works without re-deriving voter keys from a side channel. This is a deliberate simplification — a real deployment would have each voter sign with their own key. Documented in the code. The trade-off is: verification works, but the signature is not attributable to the individual voter, only to the world. Fixing this is a v0.2 concern (a "voter registration" artifact that publishes voter's public keys).
· No federation propagation of amendments. A world's law is local. C72 could carry amendments to recognizing federations; C83 doesn't.
· The _law_limits() hook in C81 is a small, additive change. It defaults to (20, 20) — preserving existing behavior. Every C81 test still passes. Only GovernedGrowingWorld overrides it.
